### panel-28 — a Button on `variant="primary"` showed a dead `cardArt` picker: component prop rows now respect variant applicability
- **Agent:** panel-designer
- **Stage:** done — PR open (draft) against `feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell`.
- **Updated:** 2026-09-16.
- **Goal:** a design-system component's prop row only shows when it actually applies to the instance's CURRENT value of the prop that gates it (Figma-style conditional rows), without ever hiding a prop the call site already sets.
- **The bug, and where it actually renders (correcting the work order's premise):** the work order's own recon pointed at `componentCallSiteRows.ts`/`ComponentSection.tsx` (the `studio.instance` "Component" section). Traced the real render path for `<Button variant="primary">` imported from `@alm-design/design-system`: `moduleMapping.ts`'s `resolveModuleId` gives it `alm.Button` (never `studio.instance` — `instanceOf` is only ever set with `source: 'local'`, confirmed in `inlineLocalComponents.ts`), so its prop rows are actually built by `src/modules/alm/register.tsx`'s `buildSchema` and rendered by `renderModuleTabContent.tsx`'s generic schema loop. **Fixed at the real location** (`register.tsx` + `renderModuleTabContent.tsx` + a new `PropertyControl.appliesWhen` field), and **also** wired the originally-named `componentCallSiteRows.ts` path for parity/future package-instance support — see "Decisions" for why that second path currently has no producer.
- **Scope:** `src/core/component-manifest/types.ts` (additive `PropSpec.appliesWhen`), `src/core/design-system-manifest/applicabilityGates.ts` (new — the prose parser, split out of `buildDesignSystemManifest.ts` to stay under the 700-line module budget), `src/core/design-system-manifest/buildDesignSystemManifest.ts` (calls the new post-pass), `src/core/module-engine/propertySchema.ts` (additive `PropertyControlBaseSchema.appliesWhen`, exported as `PropertyApplicability`), `src/core/module-engine/index.ts` + `src/core/module-engine-schema/index.ts` (barrel exports), `src/modules/alm/register.tsx` (`buildSchema` carries `PropSpec.appliesWhen` onto the control), `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/renderModuleTabContent.tsx` (new `propAppliesToInstance` check, exported for its own test), `src/admin/pages/site/property-controls/componentPropKind.ts` (additive `PropSpec.appliesWhen` + `PropApplicabilitySchema`), `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/componentCallSiteRows.ts` (`propAppliesToCallSite` filter), `src/modules/alm/manifest.generated.json` (regenerated).
- **Prose forms the parser (`applicabilityGates.ts`) handles**, each requiring every extracted token to be an exact, already-parsed enum member of exactly one OTHER prop on the same component (an ambiguous match — two props whose enums both contain the token — is a declined match, same as no match):
  1. `when prop="value"` — `Cell.toggleChecked`, `BottomActionBar.originalPrice`.
  2. `prop="value" only` — `Separator.label`.
  3. `shown by value` — `Button.cardLast4`.
  4. `<phrase> only` (phrase unnamed) — `AdBanner.showImageAction`, `MarketingCard.partnerLogoSrc`, `Search.showClose`, and the leading `AdBanner.size` ("mobile only: small | medium | large") scope-prefix form the enum cleaner already strips for the prop's own enum. `<phrase>` may be a bare `/`-joined compound (`text/payment only`) — every token must resolve to the SAME sibling enum or the match is declined.
  5. A bare `/`-joined list straight after an em/en dash, no "only" needed — `Button.cardArt` ("apple-pay / gpay-card / gpay-personalized").
- **Prose forms it deliberately declines** (a missing gate always shows the row — never derive a wrong one): a categorical phrase with no literal enum member (`Button.size`'s "text/payment only" — "text" is not a literal `variant` value; `leadingIcon`/`trailingIcon`'s "(text variants)"); `"only affects X; ignored for Y, Z"` (`AlmosaferLogo.lang` — the scope word comes AFTER "only", a grammar this parser doesn't attempt); a partial per-value exception inside an otherwise-unconditional prop (`BottomSheet.size`'s "small is iOS-only; android small → medium" — the prop applies on both platforms, only one option behaves differently, so no single `{prop, values}` gate is honest); and anything documented only in a component's SECOND usage example (`Dialog.icon`'s real "android only" comment — `parsePropComments` only reads the first fenced example, a pre-existing limit unrelated to the forms this parser can read). Also explicitly guarded against a false-positive: `AdBanner.imageSrc`'s "(mobile medium/large)" contains a literal `word/word` run whose both tokens ARE real `size` values, but it sits inside a parenthetical describing an always-applicable interpretation, not a scope — the dashed-slash-list form (5) is anchored to right-after-an-em/en-dash specifically so this never matches.
- **Result across the whole manifest:** 14 gates landed across 10 of the 39 components (`AdBanner` ×2, `BottomActionBar`, `Button` ×2 — the reported bug — `Cell` ×2, `Dialog`, `Footer`, `ListItem`, `MarketingCard`, `Search`, `Separator`, `SystemBanner`). Verified via `bun run gen-alm-manifest` (actually `bun scripts/gen-alm-manifest.mjs`) — diff is purely additive `appliesWhen` blocks, nothing else moved.
- **Decisions:**
  - **Hide the inapplicable row; never render it disabled/grayed** — per `STATE.md`'s own `panel-25` precedent (Measures section) and Rule 2 ("nothing rendered that lies").
  - **A set value always outranks a gate.** If the call site already writes the gated prop a real value (`<Button variant="primary" cardArt="/x.png">`), the row stays visible regardless of what the gate says — hiding it would make a real, live value silently un-editable and un-discoverable. Implemented identically in both render paths: `propAppliesToInstance` (`renderModuleTabContent.tsx`, checked against `resolvedPropsForBreakpoint[key]`) and `propAppliesToCallSite` (`componentCallSiteRows.ts`, checked against `callSiteProps[prop.name]`). Both check the GATED prop's own value first, before consulting the gate.
  - **`appliesWhen` is a NEW field on `PropertyControl`, kept separate from the existing `condition`/`evaluateCondition` mechanism** (`base.forms`'s mode-gated fields, `base.button`'s href-gated text already use `condition`). Reusing `condition` would mean adding the "set value outranks gate" exception to `evaluateCondition` itself, changing tested behaviour for every existing caller that doesn't need or want it. `appliesWhen`'s own check lives only in `renderModuleTabContent.tsx`'s render loop, gated on the field's presence.
  - **`componentCallSiteRows.ts`'s `appliesWhen` currently has no live producer.** `LocalComponentSpec`'s only producer is `server/handlers/studio/componentSpecExtract.ts`, a purely syntactic ts-morph `.d.ts`/type extraction with no doc-comment prose to read a gate from — a local project component genuinely has no applicability PROSE today. Wired anyway (additive schema field + `propAppliesToCallSite` filter + 3 unit tests with a hand-built spec) so a future producer (a local wrapper around a design-system component, or a package-instance manifest) has one honest place to plug into, matching the work order's explicit ask; flagging so nobody mistakes it for dead code or spends time looking for where it's populated today — it isn't, yet.
  - **`buildDesignSystemManifest.ts` split**: the new applicability parser pushed it to 833 lines, over the `module-size-budgets.test.ts` 700-line ceiling. Extracted to `src/core/design-system-manifest/applicabilityGates.ts` (210 lines, one exported function `inheritApplicability`) rather than grandfathering the budget — it was already a self-contained parsing concern with its own doc block.
- **Landmines for the next agent:**
  - `parsePropComments` (`buildDesignSystemManifest.ts`) only reads a component's FIRST fenced usage example (`firstUsageExample`) — a prop documented only in a second/alternate example (`Dialog`'s Android block) never reaches the applicability parser at all, regardless of how well-shaped its prose is. Two of my initial test assertions (`MarketingCard.centerTitle`, `Dialog.icon`) had to be dropped for exactly this reason — verify against the REAL installed package + real `buildDesignSystemManifest()` output before trusting a manual doc-string scan (I built a standalone Node script against the raw `mcp/catalog.js` first, which does NOT apply this restriction, and it overcounted).
  - A naive "any 2+ slash-joined tokens" rule is unsafe on its own — `AdBanner.imageSrc`'s "(mobile medium/large)" would have produced a real but WRONG gate (`imageSrc appliesWhen size in [medium, large]`) had the dashed-anchor restriction not been added. If extending the parser, re-run it against the FULL 39-component/199-comment corpus (dumped once via a throwaway Node script iterating `catalog.componentNames`/`catalog.apiDoc`) before trusting a new pattern — a plausible-looking regex can pass its own unit tests and still be wrong against real prose it wasn't written against.
- **Verification:** `bunx tsc -b` clean. `bun run build` clean. `bun test src/core/design-system-manifest` → 19 pass. `bun test src/__tests__/panels/componentCallSiteRows.test.ts` → 9 pass. `bun test src/__tests__/panels/propAppliesToInstance.test.ts` → 4 pass (new). `bun test src/admin/pages/site` → 935 pass / 0 fail. `bun test src/__tests__/architecture` → 549 pass / 3 fail — 2 pre-existing per the work order (`icon-catalog-integrity.test.ts` chevron-left, `no-core-barrel-deep-imports.test.ts`) **plus one more, confirmed unrelated and NOT caused by this change**: `studio-runtime-bundle-fresh.test.ts` fails in this worktree even with every change of mine `git stash`ed (worktree is 3 commits behind `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` — looks like drift from a parallel session's `studio-runtime:sync`, not this PR). `bun run lint` on the 13 files this PR touches → clean (repo-wide `bun run lint` shows 6 pre-existing `'os' is defined but never used` errors in unrelated `server/handlers/__tests__/*.test.ts` files this PR never touches).
- **Human action needed:** dogfood in `/admin/site` — open a project that imports `@alm-design/design-system`'s `Button`, select a `variant="primary"` instance, and confirm the Component/Module props no longer show `cardArt`/`cardLast4`; switch `variant` to `gpay-personalized` and confirm both rows appear (and `cardArt` renders the image picker, `cardLast4` a text box, both editable); as the one lied-about-nothing check, hand-edit the source to `<Button variant="primary" cardArt="/x.png">`, reload, and confirm `cardArt`'s row is STILL visible despite `variant` not matching the gate. Also worth a spot-check on one of the other 9 gated components (`AdBanner`'s `size`/`showImageAction` toggling `layout` is a good second case, since it exercises the scope-prefix form on the prop's OWN enum at the same time).

### panel-30 — Fill (and later Stroke/Shadow/Blur) disclosure judged on STORED, not RENDERED — "the bg is white, I don't see it in Fill" (work order)
- **Agent:** studio-architect (design, this entry) → `panel-designer` (PR1 implementation)
- **Stage:** PR1 done — draft PR [#124](https://github.com/maherfayad-stack/Figma-Killer-2/pull/124) open against `feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell`. PR2 (Stroke) / PR3 (Shadow, Blur) / PR4 (background-image layers, Content fit, shorthand) remain design-only, per Sequencing below.
- **Updated:** 2026-09-16 (PR1 implementation)
- **Roadmap:** `STUDIO-LIVE-CANVAS-PLAN.md` §P3/§P5 are both shipped (`panel-25`, `panel-26`) but this is a real defect inside what they shipped, not a new roadmap item — no plan-doc section names it. Closest kin: `docs/features/inspector.md` §5.0 (`resolveStyleFieldDisplay`, field-level prefill) and its own explicit carve-out, quoted verbatim below, which is the exact thing this ticket revisits.
- **User's own words (verbatim, from the panel's most substantive feedback so far):** *"something I can't understand is there is a lot of elements missing still like I can't see typography colors for example"*; *"some aspects of the selected element are not reflected in properties for example if I choosed body, and the bg is white I don't see that in the fill"*; *"it's not see it should show me white."* Screenshot: a selected element rendering on an obviously white background, Fill collapsed to its empty one-line header beside it.

#### Goal
One root cause, not two: **Law 1's section-open/closed decision, and the Fill list's per-row existence, are both judged ONLY on the STORED style bag** (`docs/features/inspector.md` §5.0's own words: *"Law 1's disclosure, which is judged on the STORED bag and is untouched by prefill"*) **— never on what the frame actually renders.** `FillSection.tsx`'s `setAnywhere` (the Law-1 `empty` predicate) and every row's `showXEntry` guard (`showTextEntry`/`showColorEntry`/…) read `storedStyles` exclusively; `currentStyles`/`computedValues` are computed in the same function and threaded into two popover bodies already, but never consulted for "should this section/row exist at all." So an element whose `background-color` resolves to white through an ambient/global CSS rule the parser captured but never attached to this node's `classIds` (`StyleRule.kind: 'ambient'` — `body {}`, `h1 {}`, any selector-attached rule, `src/core/page-tree/styleRule.ts`), or through simple inheritance for `color`, shows a collapsed Fill even though the canvas right next to it is plainly white. This is the field-level bug `styleFieldDisplay.ts`/`stylePlaceholder.ts` already solved once, for SCALAR always-resident sections (Measures, etc.) — Track P3's list-style sections (Fill/Stroke/Shadow/Blur) never got the same treatment because they gate on section-level presence, not per-field prefill, and nobody carried the fix across that boundary.

**"Typography colors" is the same bug, not a placement bug.** `color` is deliberately filed under Fill, not Text (`TextSection.tsx`'s own doc, G9.4: *"`color`/`textShadow` stay claimed by Fill/Shadow… a text node's colour is its fill"*) — and Penpot's own measured baseline agrees (`docs/audits/penpot-inspector-baseline/02-measurements.md` records Penpot's own Fill-section text colours, not a separate Typography-panel field). So the placement decision already made in `panel-25` stands; what's missing is that `color` on a text node with no explicit declaration ANYWHERE (the overwhelmingly common case — most `<p>`/`<span>`/`<div>` text never declares `color`, it just inherits black or the theme colour) never opens Fill's Text row, so it always reads as "no colour," which is what the user actually reported.

#### DONE WHEN (observable)
1. Select `body` (or any element) whose rendered background is a real, non-default colour with nothing in its own inline styles or assigned classes — Fill opens, shows a "Solid fill" row with the real colour, rendered in a visually distinct MUTED treatment (not indistinguishable from a stored value), and the row's popover shows that same colour.
2. Select a text-bearing element with no `color` declared anywhere — Fill opens, shows a "Text" row with the real inherited colour, muted, same treatment.
3. Select a `<div>` with no visible text and no explicit background (both computed values at their true CSS initial value: `transparent`, and — for `color` — the node has no rendered text content) — Fill stays collapsed exactly as today. **No flood**: an ordinary layout container does not sprout a Fill body just because `getComputedStyle` always returns SOME value for every property.
4. Typing a new value into a muted row commits it for real, through the SAME `resolveWriteTarget`/`commitStyle` machinery every other field already uses — no new write path. If no honest target exists (`resolveWriteTarget` returns `{kind:'none', reason}`), the popover shows that reason instead of silently eating the keystroke.
5. A stored value's row is completely unaffected — same summary, same edit, same remove button, same "N set" bookkeeping (unchanged, still judged on `storedStyles` — see Decisions).
6. `bun test src/admin/pages/site/inspector` and `bun run build` pass; the existing `fillSection.test.tsx` suite (Law 1 empty-state test included) passes unchanged.

#### Recon — what already exists and must be reused, not rebuilt
- **`PropertyProvenance`** (`panels/PropertiesPanel/stylePropertyProvenance.ts`) already carries everything needed per property: `sources` (empty when nothing declares it anywhere in the node's own class chain + inline bag), `computedValue` (ground truth from the frame), and `inherited` (true when `sources.length === 0`, a computed value exists, AND the property is in the small `INHERITED_PROPERTIES` allow-list — `color` is already in it). **`SelectionModel.provenanceByProperty` already computes this for every `ALL_CURATED_CSS_PROPERTIES` key, including all of Fill's** — `FillSection.tsx` just never reads `model.provenanceByProperty`.
- **`collapsedStyleBag.ts`'s `buildCollapsedCurrentStyles`** already merges `computedValues` under the class chain under `storedStyles` into a `currentStyles` bag `FillSection.tsx` already builds and already threads into `OrphanSatellitesBody`/`ContentFitPopoverBody` — it is simply never consulted for `setAnywhere` or the four `showXEntry` row guards.
- **`resolveWriteTarget`/`resolveExistingWriteTarget`** (`inspector/resolveWriteTarget.ts`) already do the right thing for a property with an EMPTY provenance (no stored source anywhere): fall through to the node's one writable class, else inline, else `{kind:'none', reason}`. **Nothing about the write path needs to change** — a muted row committing a new value is exactly the same call `commitApi.ts`'s `commitStyle` already makes for a totally blank field today. The only new requirement is surfacing `{kind:'none'}`'s reason in the popover instead of the current silent no-op (`commitApi.ts`'s own comment: *"the row should already be disabled by the caller when this is reachable"* — Fill's popovers don't do this yet for ANY row, stored or not; this ticket only needs to add it for the new muted rows, since a stored row by construction already has a real source and therefore a real target).
- **`resolveStyleFieldDisplay`/`stylePlaceholder.ts`** already established the exact "stored, then current-muted, then placeholder" three-tier vocabulary and the load-bearing "committing a prefilled value writes it for real; committing the SAME value writes nothing" rule — this ticket generalizes that vocabulary from scalar single-value fields to `PropertyList` ROWS, it does not invent a second one.
- **`getCSSPropertyDefaultValue`/`DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES`** (`cssControlTypes.ts`) — **looks reusable for "is this just a UA default," and is NOT.** Its own doc says it answers *"the initial value to use when ADDING a property via search"* — a UX seed value, not always the true CSS initial/computed value. Confirmed wrong for at least `objectFit` (table says `'cover'`; true CSS initial is `'fill'`) and `objectPosition` (table says `'center center'`; `getComputedStyle` normalizes to `'50% 50%'` — same value, different spelling, a naive string compare would misfire). `backgroundColor`/`backgroundImage`/`backgroundSize`/`backgroundPosition`/`backgroundRepeat`/`backgroundAttachment`/`backgroundOrigin`/`backgroundClip`/`backgroundBlendMode` DO happen to already hold their correct true-CSS-initial values in that table — but "happens to be right for 9 of 13" is not a foundation to build a correctness gate on. **Do not reuse `DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES` for the new UA-default filter** — build a small, explicit, separately-named table (see Contracts).

#### The presentation model (what a shown-but-not-stored value looks like)
Generalizes `docs/features/inspector.md` §5.0's existing three-tier rule from a scalar field to a `PropertyList` row, reusing its vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one:

1. **Stored** (today's only state): normal-weight swatch/summary, remove button present, counts toward "N set"/the indicator dot.
2. **Rendered, not stored** (new): the row exists, its swatch/summary/value read from `currentStyles`/`computedValue` instead of `storedStyles`, rendered in the panel's existing muted tone (`--text-muted`, the same token `styleFieldDisplay.ts`'s `inherited` flag already drives elsewhere — **no new token**). No remove button (there is nothing stored to remove — see Decisions). Clicking the row still opens the same popover; the field inside prefills with the rendered value, and — per §5.0's already-established rule, reused verbatim — committing it writes for real, committing the identical value writes nothing.
3. **Genuinely unset** (today's collapsed/absent state): no row at all.

`PropertyListEntry` (the shared `@ui/components/PropertyList` primitive, also used by Stroke/Shadow/Blur) needs one small additive extension to carry state (2) generically: a `muted?: boolean` flag the row renders with a muted class, and a `removable?: boolean` (default `true`) so a muted entry can suppress its own remove button without every OTHER caller having to pass one. Both are additive/optional — Stroke/Shadow/Blur's existing calls need zero changes until their own follow-up PR opts in.

#### The UA-default guard (how this avoids flooding every section)
Two different rules for two different property shapes, matching how `PropertyProvenance` already splits them:

- **Inherited properties** (`color`, `fontFamily`, … — `INHERITED_PROPERTIES` in `stylePropertyProvenance.ts`): `provenance.inherited === true` is already exactly the right signal (no source anywhere + a real computed value + the property is one CSS inherits) — reuse it as-is, no new table.
- **Non-inherited properties** (`backgroundColor`, `backgroundImage`, …): compare `computedValue` against that property's TRUE CSS initial value, normalized. When they match, the element genuinely has nothing painted — stays collapsed exactly as today. When they differ, something real is rendering that Studio cannot attribute to a stored source — show it, muted. Needs a new, small, explicitly-scoped table (see Contracts) — not `DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES` (see Recon).
- **Loading state:** while `model.computedValuesLoading` is `true` (Tier 2 bridge-mode async measure, `panel-26`), keep the OLD stored-only disclosure — do not let a not-yet-arrived `undefined` computed value either show or hide a row. Once loading resolves, re-evaluate normally. Accept the possibility of the section popping open a tick after selection on a Tier 2 board (same accepted tradeoff `panel-26`'s own "Measuring…" precedent already established elsewhere); do not build new loading chrome for this in PR1 — flag it as a dogfood follow-up if it reads as jarring.
- **Scope cut, named on purpose:** the background-image LAYER stack (`backgroundLayers.ts`'s per-layer rows), `objectFit`/`objectPosition` (Content fit), and the `background` shorthand escape hatch stay stored-only in this PR. `getComputedStyle('background-image')` returns a fully expanded, often lossy string that cannot be reliably re-parsed into an editable per-layer model the way `stylePlaceholder.ts`'s own "expansion noise" carve-out already refuses to do for shorthands generally — extending the muted-row treatment to layers is real, separate work with its own edge cases, not needed to answer the user's literal complaint (a solid background colour and a text colour), and not worth the risk in the PR that proves the mechanism.

#### Editing a shown-but-not-stored value
No new write mechanism. `resolveWriteTarget` already handles "nothing declares this property anywhere" by falling through to the node's single writable class, then inline, then `{kind:'none', reason}` — exactly the same rule that already applies to any blank field today. The one real gap: **Fill's popovers currently never check for `{kind:'none'}` and would silently no-op a keystroke** (`commitApi.ts`'s own comment says the caller is responsible for disabling this case; today's Fill never does, for any row). This ticket closes that gap for the new muted rows specifically (existing stored rows already have a real source, so a real target almost always resolves): before rendering `ColorValueInput` for a muted `text`/`color` entry, call `model.writeTargetFor(property)`; if `kind === 'none'`, render the existing `SourceConstraintNotice` component (`panels/PropertiesPanel/SourceConstraintNotice.tsx` — already the panel's established "say so, don't hide it" refusal-copy component, matching R3's "refusal as a choice in the field's own popover") with `target.reason` above the (now-disabled) colour field, instead of a silently inert control.

#### FILES
```
create  src/admin/pages/site/inspector/cssInitialValues.ts
  — new, small, explicitly-scoped table of TRUE CSS initial values for
    Fill's 13 claimed properties (backgroundColor, background, backgroundImage,
    backgroundSize, backgroundPosition, backgroundRepeat, backgroundAttachment,
    backgroundOrigin, backgroundClip, backgroundBlendMode, objectFit,
    objectPosition — color is handled via `inherited`, not this table) plus a
    normalized-equality comparator. Color-valued entries (`backgroundColor`)
    compare via `parseCssColor` (`@ui/components/ColorPickerPopover`, already
    imported by `FillSectionParts.tsx`) so `'transparent'` and
    `'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'` are recognized as equal; non-color entries fall back
    to `stylePropertyProvenance.ts`'s existing `normalizeForComparison`
    (needs exporting — see modify list). On a parse failure or an unknown
    property, default to "meaningful" (show it) — a false positive here just
    shows a real value in an unusual spelling; a false negative silently
    re-hides the exact fact this ticket exists to surface.

create  src/admin/pages/site/inspector/renderedNotStored.ts
  — the ONE shared predicate, reused by Fill now and by Stroke/Shadow/Blur in
    their own follow-up PRs (see Sequencing): `rendersUnstoredValue(provenance:
    PropertyProvenance): boolean` — false if `sources.length > 0` or
    `computedValue === undefined`; true if `inherited`; otherwise the result of
    `cssInitialValues.ts`'s comparator. Pure, no React, no store — same shape
    as `resolveWriteTarget.ts`/`resolveStyleFieldDisplay.ts`, easy to unit test
    in isolation.

modify  src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/stylePropertyProvenance.ts
  — export the existing private `normalizeForComparison` (currently
    module-private) so `cssInitialValues.ts` reuses it instead of duplicating
    a second lowercase/trim/collapse-whitespace normalizer. No behavior change.

modify  src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/FillSection.tsx
  — destructure `provenanceByProperty`, `computedValuesLoading` from
    `useSelectionModel()` (already returns both; just not read here today).
    `setAnywhere` gains an OR-branch: `!computedValuesLoading &&
    (rendersUnstoredValue(provenanceByProperty.get('backgroundColor')) ||
    (isTextNode(selectedNode) && rendersUnstoredValue(provenanceByProperty.get('color'))))`
    — `isTextNode` imported from `panels/PropertiesPanel/styleSectionOrder.ts`
    (already used by `TextSection`'s own `appliesTo`; the text-node gate is
    what stops an ordinary non-text `<div>`'s inherited black `color` from
    popping Fill open for no visible reason). `textValue`/`colorValue` each
    gain a fallback to the muted (computed) value when nothing is stored, and
    a companion `textStored`/`colorStored` boolean drives the new `muted`/
    `removable` flags on their `PropertyListEntry`. `handleRemove`'s `text`/
    `color` cases become no-ops when the entry isn't stored (defensive; the
    row shouldn't offer remove at all once `removable: false` reaches
    `PropertyList`). The `text`/`color` popover bodies gain the
    `SourceConstraintNotice` refusal check described above. Module doc comment
    updated: the existing "LAW 1 — EMPTY vs. POPULATED" section gains a
    paragraph naming the new rule and pointing at `renderedNotStored.ts`.

modify  src/ui/components/PropertyList/PropertyList.tsx (+ .module.css)
  — additive: `PropertyListEntry.muted?: boolean` (renders the row's
    label/summary/value in the muted tone, same visual language the file
    header comment for `inherited` already uses elsewhere in this panel) and
    `PropertyListEntry.removable?: boolean` (default `true`; when `false`,
    the remove button is omitted for that row, not merely disabled — nothing
    to remove). Both optional, backward compatible — Stroke/Shadow/Blur's
    existing entries compile and render byte-identical without passing
    either.

modify  docs/features/inspector.md
  — §5.0's own text ("Law 1's disclosure… is judged on the STORED bag and is
    untouched by prefill") is now false for Fill specifically; correct it in
    place, describe the new `renderedNotStored.ts` predicate, and note the
    scope boundary (Fill only today; Stroke/Shadow/Blur named as the
    follow-up). Add a short new subsection under §4 (Law 1) cross-referencing
    it, so the next reader of Law 1 doesn't re-discover this split from
    scratch.
```

#### STEPS (each leaves the tree building)
1. `cssInitialValues.ts` + its own unit test (pure table + comparator, no React) → yes.
2. Export `normalizeForComparison` from `stylePropertyProvenance.ts`; update its one new caller → yes.
3. `renderedNotStored.ts` + its own unit test (feed it hand-built `PropertyProvenance` fixtures: stored source present → false; no source, `inherited: true` → true; no source, non-inherited, computed === true initial → false; no source, non-inherited, computed !== initial → true; `computedValue: undefined` → false) → yes.
4. `PropertyList.tsx`/`.module.css` — add `muted`/`removable`, extend `PropertyList.test.tsx` with the two new cases (a muted row renders the muted class and no remove button; an un-muted row is pixel-identical to today) → yes.
5. `FillSection.tsx` — wire `renderedNotStored.ts` into `setAnywhere` and the two row guards, add the `SourceConstraintNotice` refusal check to the two popover bodies, update the module doc → yes.
6. New tests in `fillSection.test.tsx` (see Gates) — build a real iframe fixture via `registerFrameAdapter`/`PortalFrameAdapter` (the exact pattern `src/__tests__/panels/useInspectComputedStyle.test.tsx` already establishes — do not invent a second computed-style test fixture pattern) so `computedValues` is real, not `null`, then assert the four DONE-WHEN cases → yes.
7. `docs/features/inspector.md` update → yes.
8. `bun run build && bun test src/admin/pages/site/inspector src/ui/components/PropertyList && bun run lint` on the touched files.

#### CONTRACTS
```ts
// src/admin/pages/site/inspector/cssInitialValues.ts
export function isTrueCssInitialValue(
  property: keyof CSSPropertyBag,
  computedValue: string,
): boolean

// src/admin/pages/site/inspector/renderedNotStored.ts
export function rendersUnstoredValue(
  provenance: PropertyProvenance | undefined,
): boolean

// src/ui/components/PropertyList/PropertyList.tsx — additive fields only
export interface PropertyListEntry<T = unknown> {
  // …unchanged existing fields…
  muted?: boolean
  removable?: boolean // default true
}
```
No server/HTTP surface, no new store action, no new codemod, no schema change — this is a read-side (disclosure) + row-visual change only. The write path is the existing `resolveWriteTarget` → `commitApi.commitStyle` call, unchanged.

#### GATES
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/__tests__/renderedNotStored.test.ts` (new) — the four cases in Step 3.
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/__tests__/cssInitialValues.test.ts` (new) — `backgroundColor` `'transparent'`/`'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'` both read as initial; `objectFit` `'fill'` reads as initial (proving this table is NOT `DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES`, which would get this one wrong); a real non-default colour reads as non-initial.
- `src/ui/components/PropertyList/PropertyList.test.tsx` — extended with `muted`/`removable` cases.
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/__tests__/fillSection.test.tsx` — extended: (a) existing Law-1-empty test passes unchanged with no computed values registered (proves zero behavior change for the untouched path); (b) a fixture with a real `PortalFrameAdapter`-backed iframe whose CSS sets `background-color: white` on the node with nothing stored anywhere — Fill opens, shows a muted "Solid fill" row, no remove button, editing it calls `updateClassStyles`/`setNodeInlineStyles` (whichever `resolveWriteTarget` picks for that fixture) with the typed value; (c) same fixture but the fixture's writable-class/inline paths are both deliberately closed off — the popover shows `SourceConstraintNotice` with `resolveWriteTarget`'s reason, no store write fires on a keystroke; (d) an inherited, un-set `color` on a text node opens Fill's Text row muted; the SAME fixture on a non-text container (`isTextNode` false) stays collapsed even with an identical inherited computed `color`; (e) `computedValuesLoading: true` keeps the section in its old collapsed state regardless of what `computedValues` would otherwise say.
- No architecture gate needs a new rule — no banned import, no new token family (reuses `--text-muted`), no folder-layout change.

#### RISKS
- **False "meaningful" positives from an unrecognized/unparseable computed value** (e.g. a future CSS value shape `parseCssColor` doesn't understand) show a row that's technically at its default in an unusual spelling. Accepted per Decisions — favors over-showing (cosmetic noise, fixable by extending the comparator) over under-showing (the exact bug this ticket exists to close).
- **`isTextNode` false negative** (a node that visually renders text through a path the parser doesn't classify as a "text node") would keep Fill's Text row collapsed for a real inherited colour. Bounded: `isTextNode` already exists and is already trusted by `TextSection`'s own `appliesTo` gate for the identical purpose — this ticket does not need it to be more correct than that existing usage already is.
- **PropertyList's `muted`/`removable` additions are generic enough that Stroke/Shadow/Blur will eventually want them too** — if a later PR reimplements a parallel "is this row real" check instead of reusing `renderedNotStored.ts`, that is exactly the "two ways of doing something" `CLAUDE.md` bans. Named explicitly in Sequencing below so the next agent doesn't have to rediscover this.
- **Module-size**: `FillSection.tsx` is already substantial (see its own current line count before this change); adding the muted-row branches keeps it under the 700-line `module-size-budgets.test.ts` ceiling by inspection, but re-measure in Step 8, don't assume.

#### DECISIONS
- **Text colour stays in Fill.** Already decided correctly in `panel-25` (G9.4) and matches Penpot's own measured baseline (`docs/audits/penpot-inspector-baseline/`) — a text node's colour is its fill in both CSS and Penpot's own object model. The user's "I can't see typography colors" complaint is the SAME disclosure bug as the background-white complaint, not evidence the placement is wrong. Mirroring `color` into BOTH Text and Fill was considered and rejected: it would be a second, parallel place to read/write the same property, and `CLAUDE.md` explicitly bans "two ways of doing something" — one honest home, already chosen, stays.
- **Law 1's INDICATOR/"N set" count stays tied to `storedStyles` only, unchanged.** Only the `empty` (collapse) predicate and the row's existence/visual treatment change. A section popping open because something renders is not the same claim as "N properties are set here" — conflating the two would make the indicator dot lie about what's actually saved, which is the opposite of this ticket's goal.
- **A rendered-not-stored row never offers Remove.** There is nothing stored to remove; offering a disabled or fake Remove button would either do nothing (confusing) or, worse, attempt to write an explicit override (`background-color: transparent`) just to "undo" a value the user never asked to store. Editing commits for real (§5.0's existing rule, reused); there is no undo affordance beyond the ordinary "type a different value" or Ctrl+Z on whatever the user DID type.
- **Ambient-selector attribution (naming WHICH rule — `body {}`, a global stylesheet — produced the rendered value) is explicitly out of scope for this ticket.** `StyleRule.kind: 'ambient'` rules are real, parsed, first-class objects (`src/core/page-tree/styleRule.ts`) that plausibly explain many of these cases, but attributing a computed value to a specific ambient selector requires real CSS cascade/specificity matching against the DOM — a nontrivial parser feature `stylePropertyProvenance.ts`'s own doc already declines to build ("this module never resolves the CSS cascade itself"). Showing the honest computed value without claiming to know its exact source is sufficient to fix the user's actual complaint and is not a regression versus today (today shows nothing at all). Flagged as a real, worthwhile follow-up (`panel-3x`, name TBD) if a future session wants to make ambient rules directly editable from the row that renders their effect — NOT required here.
- **`DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES` is not reused for the UA-default guard**, even though it looks tempting and lives one file away — see Recon for the concrete `objectFit`/`objectPosition` mismatches that make it actively wrong for this purpose. A new, small, explicitly-scoped table is the correct move, not a shim on top of a table built for a different question.
- **Background-image layers, Content fit, and the `background` shorthand stay stored-only in this PR** — a deliberate scope cut (see the guard section above), not an oversight. Named in Sequencing as PR2/3 candidates once the mechanism is proven.

#### Sequencing (recommended, not mandated)
1. **PR1 — this ticket.** Fill only: `color` (text) + `backgroundColor` (solid fill). Proves the mechanism (`renderedNotStored.ts`, `cssInitialValues.ts`, `PropertyList`'s `muted`/`removable`, the `SourceConstraintNotice` refusal wiring) end to end on the two properties the user's own report names.
2. **PR2 — Stroke.** `borderColor`/border presence follow the identical pattern; extend `cssInitialValues.ts` with border's true initial values (`border-style: none` is already correct in `DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES` by coincidence — still re-verify, don't assume, per this ticket's own finding).
3. **PR3 — Shadow, Blur.** `boxShadow: 'none'`/`filter: 'none'` are the relevant defaults; likely the smallest of the three follow-ups since neither section has a border-style-equivalent extra axis.
4. **PR4 (optional, only if a dogfood asks for it) — Fill's background-image layer stack, Content fit, shorthand.** The scope cut named above; genuinely harder (lossy shorthand expansion), do not bundle into PR1-3.
5. **Not sequenced, explicitly deferred:** ambient-selector attribution (see Decisions).

#### PR1 — done (`panel-designer`, 2026-09-16)

Implemented exactly the scope above (`color` + `backgroundColor`, Fill only). Nothing in the FILES/CONTRACTS/DECISIONS sections above was reinterpreted; this note records what actually shipped and the two places implementation forced a call the work order left open.

**Files (matches the FILES list, plus one split forced by the line-count ceiling):**
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/cssInitialValues.ts` (new) + `__tests__/cssInitialValues.test.ts` (new)
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/renderedNotStored.ts` (new) + `__tests__/renderedNotStored.test.ts` (new)
- `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/stylePropertyProvenance.ts` — exported `normalizeForComparison`, no behavior change
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/FillSection.tsx` — wired `rendersUnstoredValue` into `setAnywhere` + the text/color row guards; module doc updated
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/FillSectionParts.tsx` — **new** `ColorPopoverField` (exported), the three-way stored/muted-writable/muted-refused popover body. Not in the original FILES list: wiring the refusal notice directly into `FillSection.tsx` pushed it to 713 lines, over the 700-line `module-size-budgets.test.ts` ceiling the RISKS section flagged as "re-measure, don't assume" — it did need splitting. `ColorPopoverField` is exactly the kind of popover-body rendering that file's own doc says belongs in `FillSectionParts.tsx`, so this is the file boundary the module already had, not a new one. `FillSection.tsx` is 668 lines, `FillSectionParts.tsx` 660, post-split.
- `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/SourceConstraintNotice.tsx` + its test — additive `writeTargetReason` prop/mode (see below)
- `src/ui/components/PropertyList/PropertyList.tsx` + `.module.css` + its test — additive `muted`/`removable` fields, exactly as specced
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/__tests__/fillSection.test.tsx` — 23 pre-existing cases pass byte-unchanged; 7 new cases (the DONE-WHEN pair plus the commit-guard, refusal, and loading-state cases)
- `docs/features/inspector.md` — §4 Law 1 and §5.0 both updated in place

**The one real design call the work order left implicit, made explicit here:** `SourceConstraintNotice`'s existing two variants (`lockReason` / `textOrigin`) each have hand-written, hardcoded prose — the structural one literally says *"This element can't be moved or deleted from here…"*. Reusing that variant verbatim for a write-target refusal (a single-PROPERTY fact, the node itself is perfectly movable) would have been wrong copy shipped to a real user. Added a third, independent, additive prop — `writeTargetReason?: string` — that renders `resolveWriteTarget`'s own reason string in its own paragraph, same visual treatment (warning-tone `.notice`, `LockSolidIcon`, "say so, don't hide it"), no invented second component. `SourceConstraintNotice`'s existing two call sites and all their tests are untouched.

**The UA-default table, as actually shipped** (`cssInitialValues.ts`) — 11 entries, each with its CSS-spec `Initial:` line cited in a comment, `color` deliberately absent (handled via `PropertyProvenance.inherited`, per the work order), `background` (the shorthand) deliberately absent (no single spec-defined initial serialization; stays stored-only this PR, so nothing ever queries it):
  `backgroundColor: 'transparent'`, `backgroundImage: 'none'`, `backgroundSize: 'auto'`, `backgroundPosition: '0% 0%'`, `backgroundRepeat: 'repeat'`, `backgroundAttachment: 'scroll'`, `backgroundOrigin: 'padding-box'`, `backgroundClip: 'border-box'`, `backgroundBlendMode: 'normal'`, `objectFit: 'fill'` (NOT `DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES`'s `'cover'`), `objectPosition: '50% 50%'` (NOT `DEFAULT_CSS_VALUES`'s `'center center'` — the exact string `getComputedStyle` reports). `backgroundColor` compares via `parseCssColor`; everything else via the newly-exported `normalizeForComparison`.

**Test fixture note for whoever writes PR2/PR3:** the DONE-WHEN pair (a rendered-but-unstored value opens the row; a genuinely-initial value doesn't) needed a REAL registered `PortalFrameAdapter` iframe, not a mocked `computedValues` prop — `useSelectionModel` reads `getComputedStyle` through the real frame-adapter registry, so there is no shallower seam. happy-dom's `getComputedStyle` does NOT resolve an undeclared non-inherited property to its true initial the way a real browser does (it returns `''`, not e.g. `'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'` for `background-color`) — inheritance (`color`) IS correctly modeled by happy-dom and needed no compensation. The fixtures therefore set the test node's OWN inline `.style.backgroundColor` explicitly to the value a real browser would have computed (`'transparent'` for the "stays collapsed" case), rather than leaving it undeclared and relying on happy-dom to resolve it — this is compensating for the test double's fidelity gap, not testing different behavior than production. The Tier 2 loading-guard test reused `useBridgeComputedValues.test.ts`'s own stub-channel pattern (`BridgeFrameAdapter` + a manually-resolved `measure` reply) trimmed to one resolve call.

**Verification:** `bun test src/admin/pages/site src/__tests__/panels src/__tests__/architecture` → 2159 pass / 2 pre-existing fail (`icon-catalog-integrity.test.ts` chevron-left, `no-core-barrel-deep-imports.test.ts` — confirmed via `git status`/diff, neither touched by this change). `bun run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) clean. `bun run lint` → the same 6 pre-existing `'os' is defined but never used'` errors this plan has logged repeatedly elsewhere, none in files this change touches. `bun test src/__tests__/architecture/module-size-budgets.test.ts` → 5 pass (both Fill files stay under the 700-line ceiling post-split).

**Rebased onto `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell`** (the Prototype-tab-sections move + the Flex-element-row spacing fix, both landed while this was in flight) — no conflicts; neither parallel change touched `FillSection.tsx`/`FillSectionParts.tsx`/`PropertyList.*`.

#### Human action needed
Dogfood against a real project. Suggested selection states, in order:

1. **Select an element (e.g. `body`, or any container) whose background colour is genuinely set only by an ambient/global rule or inherited** — nothing in its own inline styles or assigned classes. Confirm Fill now OPENS (it used to stay collapsed), shows a "Solid fill" row in a visibly muted tone with NO remove button, and that clicking it opens a popover prefilled with the real colour.
2. **In that same popover, type a new colour and blur.** Confirm it actually writes to whatever file Studio picks as the target (check the History panel / the file on disk), and the row is no longer muted afterward (it's now genuinely stored).
3. **Select a plain text element (a `<p>`/`<span>`/heading) that never explicitly declares `color` anywhere** — the overwhelmingly common case. Confirm Fill opens a muted "Text" row with the real (usually black or inherited theme) colour — this is the literal "I can't see typography colors" complaint.
4. **Select an ordinary `<div>` layout container with no background and no text of its own.** Confirm Fill stays collapsed exactly as before — no flood.
5. **If reachable:** select an element on a Tier 2 (bridge/live) board whose background is real-but-unstored, and confirm the panel doesn't flash/flicker oddly while the async measurement resolves (accepted as a possible minor jank per this ticket's own Decisions — flag if it reads as jarring, it's real follow-up work, not a PR1 blocker).

### server-21 — findScaffoldedI18n found the wrong directory in a `src/`-shaped project
- **Agent:** server-engineer
- **Stage:** done — PR [#118](https://github.com/maherfayad-stack/Figma-Killer-2/pull/118) open (draft) against `feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell`.
- **Updated:** 2026-09-16
- **Goal:** fix a real dogfooding bug — "set up locales" refused a project's Studio-written `i18n/translations.ts` + `i18n/LanguageContext.tsx` scaffold with "This project's dictionary … is not one Studio wrote," even though it was.
- **Scope:** `server/handlers/studio/i18nScaffold.ts`, `server/handlers/studio/i18nSetup.ts`, `src/__tests__/studio/i18nSetup.test.ts`.
- **Root cause:** `findScaffoldedI18n(dir)` re-derived where the scaffold "should" live from `scaffoldDir()`'s `src/`-exists heuristic (project has `src/` → guesses `src/i18n`), instead of looking beside the dictionary `readTranslationCatalog` had ALREADY resolved from the real, probed `LocalesCapability.source` (`i18n/translations.ts` at the app root, in the reported case). The guess and the fact disagreed, and the guess won — a bug, not a hypothetical.
- **The find-vs-create split (read this before touching either function again):**
  - `defaultScaffoldDir` (renamed from `scaffoldDir`) is now used **only** by `scaffoldProjectI18n` (the CREATE path). There is no dictionary yet there, so a `src/`-exists convention is the only thing to consult — that heuristic was never wrong for creation, only for lookup.
  - `findScaffoldedI18n` now takes the already-resolved `TranslationCatalog` (the caller in `i18nSetup.ts` already has it as `existing`) instead of `dir`, and derives `dirAbs = dirname(catalog.sourceAbs)` + reads `catalog.capability.source` for the posix-relative path — the dictionary's REAL location, never re-guessed. A `catalog.perLocaleFiles` catalogue (a `locales/*.json` directory) is rejected up front: Studio's own scaffold is always the two-file dictionary-module shape, never a per-locale-file directory.
  - **Do not merge these two functions or reintroduce a shared "guess a directory" helper for both paths** — one has a fact to consult, the other doesn't, and collapsing them is exactly how this bug happened the first time.
- **Hook-name strictness — decided, kept strict:** `findScaffoldedI18n` still requires the literal `export function useLanguage` in the sibling `LanguageContext.tsx`. Not loosened: the extraction codemod writes a real `import { useLanguage } from ...` statement, so it must know the hook's exact exported name rather than infer one from a renamed/re-exported variant — a wrong guess there would write an import to a symbol that may not exist. Did tighten the refusal MESSAGE in `i18nSetup.ts`, which previously asserted an authorship conclusion ("is not one Studio wrote") without saying what was actually checked; it now names the concrete fact (no Studio-generated `LanguageContext.tsx` beside the dictionary exporting `useLanguage(...)`).
- **Regression test added:** `src/__tests__/studio/i18nSetup.test.ts` — a project with both a `src/` directory (which would make the old code guess `src/i18n`) and a real Studio-written scaffold at the app-root `i18n/` is now found and extracted into, not refused.
- **Verification:** `bun test src/__tests__/studio/i18nSetup.test.ts` → 11 pass. `bun test server/handlers/studio` → 790 pass / 10 pre-existing fail (`pageWriteVerification.test.ts`'s `turnWriteLog` `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` cases — confirmed via `git status`/diff, not touched by this change). `bun test src/__tests__/studio` → 328 pass / 0 fail. `bun run build` clean (`tsc -b && vite build`). `bun run lint` → the same pre-existing 6 `'os' is defined but never used` errors this plan has logged repeatedly elsewhere (`server/handlers/__tests__/*.test.ts`, `server/handlers/studio/referenceUpload.test.ts`), none in the files this change touches.
- **Human action needed:** none — server-only fix, no UI surface changed beyond the toast message text. Worth a dogfood pass on the original repro project once convenient (open its Content panel, "set up locales") to confirm the toast no longer fires.

### panel-27 — P6: delete and gate (work order)
- **Agent:** studio-architect (design, original entry below) → test-engineer (implementation, see "Implementation" at the bottom).
- **Stage:** done — PR [#117](https://github.com/maherfayad-stack/Figma-Killer-2/pull/117) open (draft) against `feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell`. **Track P (P0–P6) is now fully shipped.**
- **Updated:** 2026-09-14.
- **Roadmap:** `STUDIO-LIVE-CANVAS-PLAN.md`, Track P, `### P6 — Delete and gate` — the last unstarted item in the track, named for `test-engineer`. Cut from `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` (P3's 11 sections + Section 11's six Studio-extras entries, and P5, are both already merged — `meta-10`, `panel-26`).
- **The plan's own P6 text is four lines and the first one is wrong.** It says `panels/PropertiesPanel/` and `property-controls/` get "removed — the 86 files." **Real count today: 148 files in `panels/PropertiesPanel/` + 37 in `property-controls/` = 185, not converging toward zero — it grew during the P3 migration, it did not shrink.** This entry is the forensic pass the plan's own text never got: a real import-graph check (`grep -rl`, not a name guess) of every one of those 185 files, done the same way `panel-25`'s "Section 11 (Studio extras)" and `panel-26`'s P5 recon already did for the files those two tickets touched. **The corrected finding: the plan's premise — "old registry, delete wholesale" — was never true of most of this folder.** The 16-entry `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` manifest (`sections/index.ts`) is a thin, new *mount* layer; almost everything it renders through (`ClassPropertyRow`, `styleValueUtils`, `stylePropertyProvenance`, `cssControlTypes`, the fill/gradient/animation/export models, `PositionConstraints`, `SizeSection`, …) is old `panels/PropertiesPanel/` code that P3 reused in place, not code P3 replaced. `property-controls/` (all 37 files) was never part of the "old CSS registry" the plan is thinking of at all — it is the generic component-prop-control layer (`ControlProps`, `PropertyControlRenderer`, the per-`componentPropKind` widgets) that both the module tab content (loop/data/component-param pickers — unrelated to CSS) and six of the new sections' own leaf controls (`ColorValueInput`, `TokenAwareInput`, `numericNudge`, `tokenUtils`) depend on. **Real deletion count: 4 files, one small cluster, plus one 1-file/1-test judgment call — not 86, not even close.**

#### Recon — the full file-by-file classification (grep-verified, not eyeballed)

Method: for every non-test `.ts`/`.tsx` in both folders, `grep -rl` for `/<basename>'` and `/<basename>"` across all of `src`, split into refs from outside the file's own directory ("ext") vs. inside it ("internal"), then manually traced every internal-only chain up to a confirmed-live root (`PropertiesPanel.tsx`, mounted from `AdminCanvasLayout/AdminCanvasEditorBody.tsx` + `RightSidebar.tsx` — both real, both outside this folder — is the one true root). Caught and corrected two false leads along the way, worth naming so nobody re-derives them the hard way:
- A same-basename collision (`CustomPropertiesSection.tsx` exists in BOTH the old folder and the new `inspector/sections/`) made the naive grep look like a false match — verified for real: the new `inspector/sections/CustomPropertiesSection.tsx` (89 lines) is a genuine wrapper around the OLD `panels/PropertiesPanel/CustomPropertiesSection.tsx` (238 lines, `import { CustomPropertiesSection as CustomPropertiesEditor } from '../../panels/PropertiesPanel/CustomPropertiesSection'`), not a duplicate — the old one is kept in place and widened with `forceOpen`, exactly as its own doc comment says. Both real, both alive.
- Generic filenames (`shared.ts`, `index.ts`) produced grep false positives against unrelated same-named files elsewhere in the tree (`framework/scaleGroups.ts`'s own `./shared`, `server/handlers/cms/plugins/shared.ts`). Re-checked with full-path-anchored greps; `property-controls/shared.ts` (the `ControlProps` type) is genuinely alive, imported by ~15 sibling control files inside its own folder — not the false-positive external refs the naive scan first reported.

**(a) Genuinely dead — safe to delete, 4 files, one cluster, nothing else touches it:**
```
delete  src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/SectionStylesMenu.tsx
delete  src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/SectionStylesMenu.module.css
delete  src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/styleFamilyClassifier.ts   — its only caller is SectionStylesMenu.tsx (dead-in-dead)
delete  src/__tests__/panels/sectionStylesMenu.test.tsx                        — the ONLY file that imports SectionStylesMenu.tsx; confirmed via `grep -rln "SectionStylesMenu"` across all of `src` (incl. `.css`) — exactly these 4 files, nothing else
```
Confirmed a per-CSS-category "Section styles" hamburger menu (reset section / add rule) from the old `StyleSectionsEditor` era with no manifest-entry equivalent and no other caller anywhere.

**(b) Ambiguous — a real judgment call, made explicitly here, not left to the implementer:**
`src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/propLockReason.ts` (48 lines, exports `propLockReason(node, propKey): string | undefined`) is imported **only** by `src/__tests__/studio/resolvedTextEditing.test.ts` — confirmed via `grep -rn "^import.*propLockReason"` across the whole tree: one hit, the test. Three other product files (`PropertiesPanelBody.tsx`, `ComponentSection.tsx`, `InPlaceInspector.tsx`) mention it BY NAME in doc comments ("R3 moved this off the string-returning `propLockReason`…") but none of them import it — it is genuinely orphaned production code, superseded by R2/R3's richer per-field messaging (`CodeValueControl`'s own hint, `SourceConstraintNotice`) sometime before this pass, not by P3. **Decision: delete `propLockReason.ts`; narrow `resolvedTextEditing.test.ts` to stop importing/asserting it, keeping every other assertion in that file** (`isPropWritableToSource`, `isPropPatchWritableToSource`, `isStyleWritableToSource`, `hasWritableSourceLocation`, `styleValueKey` — all real `@core/page-tree` exports still exercised by product code) — the file's own doc comment says it "pins the three surfaces that must agree" (store / panel / save adapter); with `propLockReason` gone, only two of those three still exist, and the file's header comment needs a one-line edit to say so, not a full rewrite.

#### RISKS

- **Bundle-size direction is real but small — do not oversell it.** Net deletion is ~4-5 files, a few hundred lines total (`SectionStylesMenu.tsx` + css + `styleFamilyClassifier.ts` + `propLockReason.ts`). `AdminCanvasEditorBody` is currently ~834–839 KB against an 850,000 B cap (`meta-10`: 834,254 B measured 2026-09-14; a later session's own number cited 839,072 B) — expect this pass to shave low-single-digit KB, not meaningfully move the needle. State the real post-change number in Step 6, do not imply this ticket "cleans up the registry" at any real size.
- **The e2e spec is the one genuinely new, nontrivial deliverable here**, not the file deletion. It needs a real dev server, real fixtures, and is the first Playwright spec that reads `docs/audits/penpot-inspector-baseline/measurements.json` programmatically — if the JSON schema drifts later, this spec breaks silently unless it validates the shape it reads (recommend a TypeBox schema for the fields it consumes, per this repo's own boundary-validation rule, since it's now a real code dependency on a hand-authored fixture file, not just prose).
- **`inspectorGeometryBudget.test.tsx`'s deletion is a rename, not a coverage loss** — every assertion moves, none are dropped. Verify with a diff before deleting the old file, not just trusting the move.
- **`resolvedTextEditing.test.ts`'s "pins the three surfaces" framing changes to two** — a real, disclosed narrowing of what the file claims to guarantee, not a silent one. If a future agent reads the old "three surfaces" language anywhere else (doc comments in `PropertiesPanelBody.tsx`/`ComponentSection.tsx`/`InPlaceInspector.tsx` that still say "propLockReason" by name, describing history) they are now referring to a deleted function — those three comments are historical/contextual, not live imports, so leaving them as-is is correct (git blame explains them), but flag: do not "fix" them by re-adding `propLockReason`.
- **The click-count e2e assertions are the most flake-prone new gate** — Playwright automation against real inputs/dropdowns can take an extra interaction a human wouldn't (e.g., a dropdown needing an explicit close click). Budget real debugging time in Step 4, don't assume the first draft passes.

#### DECISIONS

- **The plan's "86 files" premise is corrected here, not preserved.** `panels/PropertiesPanel/` and `property-controls/` are NOT a retiring registry — they are the permanent engine room six real, independent surfaces (single-node CSS sections, multi-select, ambient/global selector, VC instance view, class management, module-tab content) all still mount through. Both folders keep their names and locations. This is a real correction to Track P's own plan text, made explicit here so nobody re-attempts a wholesale purge later based on the stale "86 files" line.
- **`inspectorGeometryBudget.test.tsx` is moved, not kept alongside the new file** — two tests both named "the measurement gate" with overlapping content is exactly the "old and new side by side" this repo's rules ban, even though the plan's literal path (`src/__tests__/inspector/measurement.test.ts`) differs from the existing file's location.
- **The real per-section-height and click-count assertions are Playwright (`tests/e2e/`), not `bun test`** — `happy-dom` does not lay out the DOM (already proven once, by `inspectorGeometryBudget.test.tsx`'s own header comment); re-deriving this the hard way would waste a full implementation cycle. The plan's literal file path (`src/__tests__/inspector/measurement.test.ts`) is kept for the static/manifest half only; the real half gets its own e2e spec, named explicitly here so the split isn't rediscovered mid-implementation.
- **The click-count claim IS automatable**, contradicting this ticket's own dispatch prompt's suggested fallback ("recommend the honest alternative: a documented manual dogfood checklist") — the P0 baseline already recorded the numbers (`clickCountsToCommonEdit`), so a real Playwright spec can drive the same flows and count real interactions. Manual dogfood is reserved for the two things the baseline ITSELF couldn't automate (the color popover, explicitly noted as a failed capture) and the qualitative "feel" of control placement — not the click counts.
- **`propLockReason.ts` deletion is judged, not deferred** — orphaned by an earlier pass (R2/R3), not by P3, but P6's own charter is "delete and gate" for this folder as a whole, not scoped only to P3-caused dead code; leaving a tested-but-uncalled function in place because "some other ticket introduced the orphaning" is exactly the kind of TODO this repo's own rules forbid.

**DELEGATE TO:** `test-engineer` (the plan's own named P6 owner — confirmed still the right fit: the deliverable is two test files and a doc rewrite, no CSS/canvas/store surface work). If the e2e fixture setup turns out to need new Studio-side board/frame scaffolding beyond what `tests/e2e/`'s existing helpers already provide, that sub-piece may want a `canvas-engineer` pass first — flag, don't block on it up front.

#### Implementation (test-engineer)

Followed the work order's own 6-step build order exactly, cut from `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` via `.tmp/wt-panel-27-delete-gate` (`git worktree add ... -b feat/panel-delete-gate`). Build/test green at every step, per the work order's own discipline.

- **Steps 1–2 (deletion + `data-section-id`):** exactly the 4 files + `propLockReason.ts`, no more, no less. Confirmed via grep before and after that nothing else referenced any of them. **Real, unpredicted finding on bundle size**: `AdminCanvasEditorBody` was **byte-identical** before and after the deletion (839,072 B, same content hash) — the deleted files were reachable ONLY from their own test file, so Vite had already tree-shaken them out of the production bundle; the Risks section's own "expect low-single-digit KB" prediction assumed they were shipping, and they weren't. The two new additive testids (Step 2) added the entire real delta: final build **839,164 B** (+92 B net), still far under the 850,000 B cap.
- **Step 3 (static measurement.test.ts):** moved+widened cleanly — every `inspectorGeometryBudget.test.tsx` assertion carried over unchanged, glob widened to `inspector/sections/**/*.module.css`. Added the 16-entry manifest-shape checks and a computed per-section rest-height table. **Real, unpredicted finding**: building the per-section row-count table required reading each of the 16 sections' own source for real (not guessable) — `Layer`/`Align`/`Measures` are headerless (Penpot's unlabeled top rows), `Fill`/`Stroke`/`Shadow`/`Blur`/`Export`/`Transform`/`Animations`/`Interaction` all collapse to a 0-row empty header via `Section`'s `empty` prop (Law 1), `Text` is explicitly documented as always-resident 4 rows, `Attributes`/`CustomProperties` each carry a 1-row "Add" affordance even when empty. All 12 static tests pass.
- **Step 4 (the e2e spec — the real, nontrivial deliverable, budgeted real debugging time as warned):**
  - **First real blocker, not anticipated by the work order**: `css-writeback.e2e.ts`'s own documented fixture convention (an OS temp dir opened by absolute path, "the studio dir resolver accepts one") is **stale** — `resolveProjectDir` (`server/handlers/studioProjects.ts`) now containment-checks every `dir` against `projectsRootDir()` (a real W10 security hardening pass that landed after that spec's comment was written). Reproduced the exact same "Could not open this project — Not found" failure against `css-writeback.e2e.ts`'s own fixture to confirm this is real drift, not a bug in this spec's own setup, before switching to `canvas-06-sheet-render-fidelity.e2e.ts`'s convention instead — a throwaway project genuinely inside `studio-workspace/`, created fresh under a `panel27-e2e-<random>` name and removed in `afterAll`.
  - **Second blocker**: the canvas's own zoom-to-fit pan does not reliably center a freshly-opened project's frame — the frame's own origin measured `x < 0` (off-screen left) before any panning. Adopted `canvas-06`'s own `panIntoView` helper rather than assuming visibility.
