### panel-26 — P5: values from the live DOM (work order)
- **Agent:** studio-architect (design, this entry's original text below) → panel-designer (implementation, see "Implementation" at the bottom)
- **Stage:** done — PR #116 open (draft) against `feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell`
- **Updated:** 2026-09-14
- **Roadmap:** `STUDIO-LIVE-CANVAS-PLAN.md` §P5 (between P4/`panel-23`, already shipped, and P6/`test-engineer`'s deletion pass, not yet started). P5's own plan text is three lines: "`SelectionModel`'s effective values read through `adapter.measure` at Tier 2; Tier 0 keeps the registry-computed path. One call site." **That framing undercounts badly and is stale against what P3/P4 actually built** — see Recon below. Cut from `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` (P3's Section 11 / P4 are both already on it, per `meta-10`).
- **Goal:** the Properties Panel's computed-style read (`useFrameComputedStyleValues`/`useInspectComputedStyle`, `panels/InspectPanel/useInspectComputedStyle.ts`) currently bypasses `FrameDocumentAdapter` entirely and reaches `frame.contentDocument`/`getComputedStyle` directly — which silently returns nothing for a Tier 2 bridge-mode frame (cross-origin, no `contentDocument` access; the existing `try/catch` swallows the `DOMException` and returns `null`). **Done when:** selecting a node in a Tier 2 (`documentMode='bridge'`) board frame shows real computed values in Measures/Fill/Stroke/Layer/Layout/Text/Transform/Interaction/Export sections and the Inspect tab, sourced via the already-built `adapter.measure()`/`findRenderedCanvasNodes` path — with a bounded "measuring…" loading state, never a silent blank — while every Tier 0/1 (portal) board keeps the exact byte-identical synchronous read it has today, proven by the existing pinned test suite passing unchanged.
- **DONE WHEN (observable):** a Tier 2 dev-server board, once dogfoodable (L6+ is shipped but Track L's own "genuinely testable only against a real running dev server" caveat still applies — see live-05's own Verification-strategy split), shows live `getComputedStyle` values in the Properties Panel for a selected node within ~2s (the existing `BridgeFrameAdapter` measure timeout) of selection, with a visible loading affordance during that window; a Tier 0/1 board's Properties Panel is provably unchanged (existing `useInspectComputedStyle.test.tsx` passes with zero behavioral assertions changed, only the wrapper shape).

#### Recon — the plan's "one call site" framing, checked against the current tree, not assumed

**It undercounts. There are 6 files with direct hook-invocation call sites, not 1**, plus ~19 files that consume the *value* one hop downstream through `SelectionModel` (unaffected if the design below is followed — see "Why the blast radius shrank" below). Grepped `useFrameComputedStyleValues`/`useInspectComputedStyle` across the current tree (not the stale `live-05`-era doc comment inside the hook's own file, which lists a 9-file consumer set that predates all of P3):

1. **`src/admin/pages/site/inspector/selectionModel.ts:186`** — the P4 `SelectionModel`'s own call, `useFrameComputedStyleValues(selectedNodeId, activeBreakpointId ?? 'desktop', ALL_CURATED_CSS_PROPERTIES)`. This is genuinely the plan's "one call site" for the *SelectionModel's* own path — P4 really did centralize it, the plan's gloss just doesn't know P4 shipped since.
2. **`src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/AlignSection.tsx:103`** — a SECOND, independent call for the selected node's *parent's* computed `display`/`flexDirection` (align-row eligibility). Bypasses `SelectionModel` entirely — the parent isn't the selection.
3. **`src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/ConstraintsDiagram.tsx:96-97`** — TWO more calls (`nodeComputed`, `parentComputed`), for the constraints crosshair's positioned-context/geometry math. Reached via `MeasuresSection.tsx` (P3, live) → `PositionConstraints.tsx` (old `panels/PropertiesPanel/` file, confirmed **still live and reused, not dead code awaiting P6** — `MeasuresSection.tsx`'s own doc comment says so explicitly: "ported from the retired `PositionSection.tsx`... ConstraintsDiagram... F29's side pickers + crosshair) already cover that honestly").
4. **`src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/useSizingParentLayout.ts:53`** — the Hug/Fill sizing model's own parent-layout read, called only from `MeasuresSection.tsx` (`sizingParent = useSizingParentLayout()`).
5. **`src/admin/pages/site/panels/InspectPanel/InspectPanel.tsx:56`** — the separate **Inspect tab** (read-only "what actually rendered" report, `InspectorShell`'s third tab), calling the sibling hook `useInspectComputedStyle` (fixed-shape `ComputedStyleSnapshot`, not the curated-properties bag).
6. `selectionModel.ts` again is the only SelectionModel-side call — confirmed by grepping `useFrameComputedStyleValues(` literally (not just the import) across the tree: exactly 5 real invocations total across 1+4 other files (`selectionModel.ts` ×1, `AlignSection.tsx` ×1, `ConstraintsDiagram.tsx` ×2, `useSizingParentLayout.ts` ×1), plus `InspectPanel.tsx`'s ×1 call to the sibling hook. **6 files, 6 call sites total** (not counting the hook's own definition file or its test).

**Downstream-of-SelectionModel consumers (do NOT call the hook directly — read `useSelectionModel()`'s already-derived `computedValues`/`provenanceByProperty` fields):** grepped every real `useSelectionModel()` call site in the current tree — **19 files**: all 11 `inspector/sections/*.tsx` P3 section components (`LayerSection`, `AlignSection`, `MeasuresSection`, `LayoutSection`, `FillSection`, `StrokeSection`, `ShadowSection`, `BlurSection`, `TextSection`, `ExportSection`, plus the Section-11 group `ComponentSection`/`AttributesSection`/`TransformSection`/`AnimationsSection`/`InteractionSection`/`CustomPropertiesSection`), `StyleSurface.tsx`, `StyleRuleComposer.tsx`, `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx`, `usePropertiesPanelData.ts`, `PropertiesPanelBody.tsx`. Of these, only **9 actually read `computedValues`/`provenanceByProperty`** (confirmed by grep, not assumed): `ExportSection` (provenance only), `FillSection`, `InteractionSection`, `LayerSection`, `LayoutSection`, `MeasuresSection`, `StrokeSection`, `TextSection`, `TransformSection`. `StyleSurface.tsx` itself only reads `selectedNodeId`/`selectedNode`/`assignedClassRules`/`writableClasses`/`inlineWritable`/`inlineLockReason` from the model — not the computed-style fields — despite its own doc comment listing them among what it "used to compute" (P4 moved that computation into the manifest sections, correctly; the doc comment is describing history, not current reads).

**Why the blast radius shrinks back down, if the hook's own return-shape change is absorbed at the right boundary:** none of those 19 (or their 9-of-19 computed-value-reading subset) need to change AT ALL if `selectionModel.ts` is the ONE place that unwraps the hook's new `{ value, isLoading }` shape back into today's existing `computedValues: Record<string,string> | null` field (unchanged name, unchanged shape, unchanged meaning), plus one new, purely additive `computedValuesLoading: boolean` field a section MAY read and none is required to. **This is a real, deliberate revision of the `live-05`-era design** (STATE.md, `live-05`'s fourth-session entry, "Concrete shape: both hooks change return type... Caller updates required in the same change: the Inspect tab's... and `StyleSurface`'s provenance-by-property calculation... both switch from treating the return as a plain record to reading `.value`/`.isLoading`") — that note was written before P3/P4 existed, when `StyleSurface` itself still computed `provenanceByProperty` inline (per that note's own premise). P4 already inserted exactly the seam (`SelectionModel`) that makes the propagation-to-9-files unnecessary. Re-checked, not assumed: verified `StyleSurface.tsx`'s CURRENT code (P4-rewired) does not read `computedValues` at all, and every one of the 9 section files reads it only via `model.computedValues`/`model.provenanceByProperty`, never by calling the hook itself.

**Real total scope: 6 files get their hook-call-site code changed** (`selectionModel.ts`, `AlignSection.tsx`, `ConstraintsDiagram.tsx`, `useSizingParentLayout.ts`, `InspectPanel.tsx`, plus the hook's own definition file `useInspectComputedStyle.ts`), **0 files need a shape-change edit two hops downstream.**

#### Recon — resolving the portal-mode ambiguity precisely (task question 2)

Read `FrameDocumentAdapter.measure()`'s contract and both real implementations:

- **`useInspectComputedStyle.ts` does NOT call `adapter.measure()` today, in either mode.** It reads `frame.contentDocument?.body` directly (`frameBodyElement`, wrapped in a `try/catch` that silently returns `null` on the cross-origin `DOMException` a bridge frame would throw) and calls `view.getComputedStyle(element)` directly, via its own `RenderedCanvasNodeCache` (`canvasNodeLookup.ts`) — a portal-only mechanism, confirmed by reading every line of the file. It bypasses `FrameDocumentAdapter` entirely; this is a real, separate reach-in that `frame-document-adapter-isolation.test.ts`'s narrowed `BANNED_PATTERNS` (literal `.contentDocument`/`.contentWindow` property reads only, per `live-05`'s fifth session) does not currently catch because `useInspectComputedStyle.ts` sits under `panels/InspectPanel/`, outside the gate's `canvas/**` glob — worth flagging to whoever owns that gate's scope, not this ticket's job to widen.
- **`PortalFrameAdapter.measure()` is real, exists, and IS `Promise`-shaped** (`async measure(...)`, no internal `await` — resolves on the next microtask, not literally synchronously to the caller). It is simply not what this hook calls. Even if it were routed through the adapter, a microtask-deferred resolution is enough of a real timing change to break the hook's own documented "same-tick, zero extra re-render" contract for the highest-keystroke-frequency surface in the panel.
- **Resolution: "Tier 0 keeps the registry-computed path" means keep the existing direct DOM reach-in for portal mode, byte-identical, not "route portal mode through `adapter.measure` since it happens to resolve fast."** The portal branch of both hooks is UNCHANGED by this work order except for the return-value wrapper (`{ value: <today's result>, isLoading: false }`). This is a corrected reading of the plan's own three-line gloss, not a new decision this ticket is inventing — confirmed by reading the actual adapter code, not inferred from the plan text alone.

#### Recon — the bridge-mode read already has almost everything it needs built

`canvasNodeLookup.ts` (Class A/B split, `live-05`'s fifth session) already has the exact cross-mode primitive this ticket needs, sitting unused by any Properties Panel caller:

```ts
// already exists, unchanged by this ticket
export async function findRenderedCanvasNodes(
  nodeId: string,
  properties?: string[],
): Promise<RenderedCanvasNode[]>   // RenderedCanvasNode = { rect: NodeRect; computedStyle: Record<string,string>; frame: HTMLIFrameElement }
```

It iterates `listFrameAdapters()` (the module-scoped registry every `IframeFrameSurface` registers into on mount, portal AND bridge alike) and calls `adapter.measure([{nodeId}], properties)` on each — genuinely mode-agnostic, already built, already tested (`canvasNodeLookup.test.ts`), **zero new wire messages needed** (unlike every other `live-05` gap, which needed a new `OutboundRuntimeMessage`/`FrameRuntimeEvent` variant — `occurrenceIndex`, `frame:resize`, the still-undesigned `selection:reflow`). This is the one genuinely good-news finding of this recon: **P5's own wire-protocol footprint is zero**, so it does NOT need to join `live-05`'s 5-item "wire-protocol security-review queue" (STATE.md, `live-05` Landmines, repeatedly re-flagged across 5 sessions, none of the 4 pending items built yet) — `MeasureMessageSchema` already shipped and was already reviewed (`sec-06`); P5 is simply this schema's first real production caller.

**The one real gap:** picking WHICH registered frame's result to prefer when a node renders in more than one open breakpoint frame (mirroring the portal-only `pickPreferredElement`'s "prefer the frame whose `data-breakpoint-id` matches the active breakpoint" rule, `useInspectComputedStyle.ts:118-127`). That function reads `frame.contentDocument?.body`'s `data-breakpoint-id` attribute — impossible cross-origin for a bridge frame. **Fix, verified against `IframeFrameSurface.tsx`'s real JSX:** neither `documentMode` branch's `<iframe>` element carries `data-breakpoint-id` on ITSELF today — only the portal branch's `srcDoc` document's `<body>` gets it (via `applyIframeBodyReset`, unreachable cross-origin). Stamping `data-breakpoint-id={breakpointId}` directly onto the outer `<iframe>` in BOTH branches is a trivial, additive, zero-risk change (an extra `data-*` attribute the isolation gate doesn't scan for, the CSS `[data-breakpoint-id="…"]`-scoped selectors don't target since they're scoped to elements INSIDE the frame document, not the iframe element itself) that gives any caller holding an `HTMLIFrameElement` — including `RenderedCanvasNode.frame` — a same-origin-readable way to know which breakpoint it represents, in EITHER mode.

#### Design — the actual shape (a real revision of the `live-05`-era note, not a re-statement of it)

1. **`useInspectComputedStyle.ts` — both exported hooks change return type from `T | null` to `{ value: T | null; isLoading: boolean }`.** Portal-mode internals are 100% unchanged (`RenderedCanvasNodeCache`, `stabilizeRecord`, the synchronous `getComputedStyle` read) — only the return statement's wrapper changes, and `isLoading` is a hardcoded `false` literal on that path. This is what makes "Tier 0/1 boards take ZERO new code paths" true at the hook's own boundary, not just at the SelectionModel's.
2. **New file `panels/InspectPanel/useBridgeComputedValues.ts`** — kept OUT of `useInspectComputedStyle.ts` itself (already 308 lines of dense, already-written doc/logic; a `no-vc-mode-branches`-style "one reason per module" split, not a budget dodge) — exports:
   - `hasBridgeFrameFor(breakpointId: string): boolean` — `for (const [frame, adapter] of listFrameAdapters()) if (isBridgeFrameAdapter(adapter) && frame.getAttribute('data-breakpoint-id') === breakpointId) return true; return false`. **Uses `isBridgeFrameAdapter` (from `BridgeFrameAdapter.ts`), not `isPortalFrameAdapter`** — `meta-10`'s own import-cycle finding (`BridgeFrameAdapter.ts` has zero store-import chain; `PortalFrameAdapter.ts`'s chain does) is the reason to keep that direction consistent here too, even though this file doesn't sit in the same import path that tripped the original cycle — cheap insurance, same precedent.
   - `useBridgeComputedValues(nodeId, breakpointId, properties, active): { value: Record<string,string> | null; isLoading: boolean }` — a REAL hook (`useState` for the last-resolved snapshot + a monotonic generation counter in a plain `useRef` — read/written only inside the effect/callback, never during render, so it's a legitimate ref use, not a `useMutableBox` case; `useEffect` keyed on `[nodeId, breakpointId, properties, active]`). Called UNCONDITIONALLY from both exported hooks (Rules of Hooks), but its own effect body no-ops immediately when `active` is `false` — so for every Tier 0/1 render this is an extra mounted-but-permanently-inert `useState`/`useRef`/`useEffect` triple, executing zero logic and producing zero observable difference. This is the same "always-mounted, mode-gated no-op" pattern `useIframeFrameAutoHeight.ts`'s own bridge branch already uses (`live-05`, Batch 5) — not a new pattern this ticket invents.
   - On a real firing: bump generation, call `preferredRenderedCanvasNode(nodeId, breakpointId, properties)` (new export on `canvasNodeLookup.ts`, see below), `isLoading: true` until it settles. On resolve, apply only if the generation still matches the latest fired request (stale resolutions silently dropped — no cancellation API needed, `BridgeFrameAdapter.measure()` already bounds every request to 2000ms, matching the `frame:resize` precedent's "bounded, self-healing" tolerance). While in flight, `value` stays the PREVIOUS resolved snapshot (never flickers to `null` mid-typing); a timeout (rejected promise) sets `isLoading: false` and keeps the previous value, silently — the codemod/measure call already has its own bounded-timeout contract, nothing new to design there.
3. **`canvasNodeLookup.ts` gains one export, no other changes:**
   ```ts

#### Risks

- **Bundle-size headroom is real but tight.** `AdminCanvasEditorBody` measured 836.17 kB after P3 Section 11 (`panel-25`'s last entry) against an 850,000 B cap — **~13.8 KB of headroom**. This ticket adds one new file (`useBridgeComputedValues.ts`, expect 100-150 lines of real logic — small) plus a handful of unwrap-site edits (near-zero net new bytes at those 5 call sites) — should comfortably fit, but **re-measure for real in Step 7, do not assume**; if it doesn't fit, the correct move is the same one every P3 section already used (ratchet the cap with a one-line dated justification, not defer or shrink the feature).
- **`MeasureMessageSchema.properties` has no `maxItems` bound today**, and `ALL_CURATED_CSS_PROPERTIES` (~90 entries) becomes this schema's first real production payload of meaningful size once `selectionModel.ts`'s bridge branch fires — previously only test fixtures and small, hand-picked property lists (`AlignSection`'s 2, `ConstraintsDiagram`'s handful) ever exercised it. Not a new vulnerability this ticket introduces (the schema already validates every element is a non-empty string, and the array arrives over a `postMessage` channel already gated by `BridgeFrameAdapter`'s own origin check), but worth a `security-guard` look specifically because it's the schema's first real-scale caller — recommend flagging in the same short follow-up review `live-05`'s own queue already asks for on `occurrenceIndex`/`frame:resize`, not blocking this ticket on it (this ticket adds no NEW wire message — see Recon above — so it is not obligated to join that queue by this repo's own precedent, but a second pair of eyes on the payload SIZE, as opposed to shape, is cheap and worth asking for).
- **The generation-counter guard is the one genuinely new piece of async-correctness logic in this whole ticket** — get it wrong and a fast re-selection (node A → node B before A's measure resolves) could apply A's stale values under B's selection. Mitigated by testing it explicitly and directly (see Gates) rather than trusting it by inspection, and by reusing the exact pattern the deferred `live-05` design already worked out for this (STATE.md, `live-05` fourth session) — not inventing a new one.
- **`useSizingParentLayout.test.ts`/`inspectPanel.test.tsx` are both NEW test files for previously-untested components** — real, disclosed scope, not silently skipped; both are small (the hook is 84 lines today, the panel 273), not a hidden multi-day tax.
- **Module-size**: none of the 7 touched/created files approach the 700-line `module-size-budgets.test.ts` ceiling (`useInspectComputedStyle.ts` 308 today, `canvasNodeLookup.ts` 480, everything else under 275) — checked, not assumed.

#### Decisions
- **The `live-05`-era `{value, isLoading}` design (STATE.md, `live-05` 4th session) is correct in its return-shape choice and WRONG in its propagation scope** — that note predates P3/P4 and assumed every consumer needed to change. Re-verified against the current tree: `SelectionModel` (P4) already IS the seam that absorbs the shape change for 19 downstream files (9 of which genuinely read the value) at zero cost to them. Only the 6 files with a DIRECT hook-invocation call site change.
- **Portal mode keeps its existing direct-DOM reach-in, unrouted through `adapter.measure()`**, even though `PortalFrameAdapter.measure()` exists and is nominally `Promise`-shaped — confirmed by reading both adapter implementations, not inferred. A microtask-deferred resolution is a real timing regression against this hook's own documented zero-extra-re-render contract for the highest-keystroke-frequency surface in the panel; not worth it for a same-process read that already works.
- **No new wire message.** `MeasureMessageSchema`/`MeasureResultMessageSchema` already carry everything this ticket needs (`properties?: string[]` in, `computedStyle: Record<string,string>` out) — confirmed by reading `messages.ts`. This keeps P5 OUT of `live-05`'s standing wire-protocol security-review queue by construction, not by omission.
- **`data-breakpoint-id` moves from "portal body only" to "outer iframe element, both modes."** Chosen over inventing a NEW way to carry breakpoint identity across the bridge boundary (e.g. echoing it back in every `measure:result`) because the fact is already known synchronously and locally by the exact React component (`IframeFrameSurface`) that already renders the `breakpointId` prop onto something — moving it one DOM level up costs one JSX attribute and needs no wire-protocol change at all.
- **`useBridgeComputedValues.ts` is a new, separate file, not more code stuffed into `useInspectComputedStyle.ts`.** That file is already dense (308 lines of prose-heavy, already-carefully-written doc comments the module doc itself calls out as load-bearing) — matches this repo's "one reason per module" rule better than growing it further.
- **`computedValuesLoading` is additive-only on `SelectionModel`** — no existing field renamed or removed, so every one of P4's own 3 test files (`commitApi.test.ts`, `selectionModel.test.ts`, the RTL suites) that destructure the model without this field keeps compiling and passing unchanged (TypeScript structural typing doesn't require callers to destructure every field).

#### Human action needed
None blocking — this design is directly implementable by `panel-designer` (the plan's own named owner for P5) from this entry, the same "nothing above is gated on a further human decision" posture `live-05`'s own Batch-4 resolution used. One thing worth a human call, not a blocker: whether `ConstraintsDiagram.tsx`'s crosshair should show an explicit "measuring…" affordance during a bridge-mode in-flight read, or silently render its existing "can't compute yet" state until the value resolves (this entry chose the latter, minimum-surface-area option — see Design item 7 — a `panel-designer` call to revisit if a dogfood session finds the crosshair popping in jarringly once L6+ is truly dogfoodable).

#### Implementation (panel-designer)
- **Followed the 7-step build order exactly** — steps 1-3 (`preferredRenderedCanvasNode` + test, `data-breakpoint-id` on both `IframeFrameSurface.tsx` branches, `useBridgeComputedValues.ts` + test) each landed additive-only and green in isolation; steps 4-6 (the hook's own `{value,isLoading}` signature change + all 5 direct callers) went in as one commit, exactly as the compile-time constraint required. Cut from `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` via `.tmp/wt-panel-26-live-dom` (`git worktree add ... -b feat/panel-live-dom-values`).
- **One real gap the design's own step 3 didn't spell out, found and fixed during implementation:** the curated property lists every existing caller passes (`ALL_CURATED_CSS_PROPERTIES`, `AlignSection`'s `['display','flexDirection']`, etc.) are camelCase — the same `CSSStyleDeclaration` accessor vocabulary the portal branch's direct `cs[prop]` read uses. The `measure` wire message and both adapters' own `getPropertyValue` calls (`runtime.ts`/`PortalFrameAdapter.ts`'s `DEFAULT_MEASURED_PROPERTIES`) are kebab-case — `getPropertyValue('flexDirection')` silently returns `''`. `useBridgeComputedValues.ts` now converts camelCase -> kebab-case before the wire call (via `camelToKebabCssProperty`, `@core/css-codemods`) and re-keys the reply back to camelCase before returning — the one place that bridges the two vocabularies, tested directly (`useBridgeComputedValues.test.ts`'s "requests kebab-case wire properties and returns the reply re-keyed back to camelCase").
- **One lint fix beyond the design's own text:** the naive `setIsLoading(true)` called directly and synchronously in the effect body tripped `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`. Fixed by wrapping the whole measure-start body in `useEffectEvent` (mirroring `useAsyncResource.ts`'s own `runLoad` pattern exactly — the established precedent in this codebase for this exact lint rule), with every value the request needs passed as an explicit parameter (not read off the closure) so it stays the value the effect captured when it fired, not `useEffectEvent`'s "always latest" substitute.

#### Read this first — what P1/P2/P4 actually shipped (their own STATE.md entries are long; this is what P3 needs from them)

- **The manifest mechanism (`panel-23` Phase B) is real and this is the ONLY thing P3 touches to add a section:** `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/index.ts` exports `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS: InspectorSectionDefinition[]`, currently ONE entry (`{ id: 'styles', order: 0, appliesTo: () => true, Component: StyleSectionsComposer }`). `StyleSurface.tsx` already mounts `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS.filter((s) => s.appliesTo(model)).sort((a,b) => a.order - b.order).map((s) => <s.Component key={s.id} />)` — confirmed by reading the file, not assumed. **Never touch `StyleSurface.tsx`'s mount loop itself** — growing the array is the whole job.
- **`useSelectionModel()`/`useInspectorCommit(model)` (`src/admin/pages/site/inspector/{selectionModel,commitApi}.ts`) are the ONLY store surface a new section may read/write through.** Every new section component calls `const model = useSelectionModel(); const commit = useInspectorCommit(model)` and uses `model.selectedNode`/`model.assignedClassRules`/`model.provenanceByProperty`/`model.computedValues`/`commit.commitStyle`/`commit.commitStyleMany`/`commit.commitProp`. Do not call `resolveWriteTarget`/raw store style actions directly from a section — that is exactly the "25 ad-hoc commit paths" P4 deleted; a new section reintroducing one is a straight regression of P4's own work.

Apply these four **now, globally, as a single Step 0 change** — they are pure 1:1 value corrections (the token already means the same thing, just the wrong number), not a restructuring, so every section (migrated or not) becomes visually more Penpot-accurate immediately. --inspector-accent-dark: #7EFFF5;   /* teal */
--inspector-accent-light: #6911D4;  /* purple — hue changes per theme, not just lightness */
--inspector-field-bg: #212426;      /* dark; #F3F4F6 light — redefine, don't reuse --overlay-5 */
--inspector-section-label-color: #8F9DA3; /* dark; #495E74 light */
```
Resolve these through the existing `:root`/`[data-theme='light']` (or equivalent) split `globals.css` already uses for every other dual-value token — read the file's own pattern for `--text-*`/`--bg-*` before adding these, do not invent a new mechanism for per-theme tokens.

**The Rule-2 gap — found during this design, not previously documented:** `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` reads a persisted preference (`propertiesSectionsExpanded`, `preferences/catalog.ts`) and passes it as `Section`'s `defaultOpen` for every `collapsedWhenEmpty` section (fill/border/effects/animations/typography/interaction — 6 of the 11 old sections) — meaning a user can manually collapse a POPULATED section today via `Section.tsx`'s hover-revealed chevron, and that collapse persists. This is a real, live violation of P2 rule 2 ("Everything is at rest. No accordion to open.") that neither `panel-21` nor `panel-22` caught (`panel-21`'s own "Module section un-accordioned" note was about the CMS module settings block, not this). **`Section.tsx` itself does NOT need to change** — it already has a `forceOpen` prop that, combined with `empty={<nothing set>}`, gives exactly "one static header line when empty, always-expanded with no chevron once populated" (confirmed by reading `Section.tsx:60-140`: `forceOpen` suppresses both the toggle button's click handler and the chevron glyph). **Every new Penpot section this work order builds must pass `forceOpen` and must never read `propertiesSectionsExpanded`.** `Section.tsx` is also used by `GitPanel`/`FrameworkScalePanel` (ordinary admin panels, not the Penpot-modeled inspector) — do not change its default behavior globally, only how the 11 new sections call it. `propertiesSectionsExpanded` (`catalog.ts`) and its `useEditorPreference` read in `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx`/`CustomPropertiesSection.tsx` get deleted in whichever PR deletes the LAST of those two files (Studio extras, item 11, or P6 if any straggler remains).

#### The 11-section mapping — every old file accounted for, nothing silently dropped

The plan's own item list (§P3) names 11 sections but the CURRENT tree has 11 CSS-category sections (`classStyleSections.ts`'s `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS`: position/size/layout/spacing/appearance/fill/border/effects/animations/typography/interaction) **plus 4 node-level panels** (Export, ComponentParamsOverview, InstanceCallSiteView, HtmlAttributesPanel) that live outside that registry. Mapping old → new is not 1:1 — three old categories (spacing/animations/interaction) and two node-level panels plus one old section's leftover popover have no named Penpot section to land in at all, because Penpot has no concept for them. Resolving that silently would be a feature loss; resolving it explicitly is this table:

| # | New section (Penpot order) | Pulls from (old files) | Properties/concerns claimed | Key P0 finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Layer** | NEW — see full template below. `AppearanceSection.tsx`'s opacity + `AppearanceSectionActions`' blend-mode trigger. Structural hide/lock are NEW UI (see template). | `opacity`, `mixBlendMode`, node.`hidden`, node.`locked` | `02-measurements.md`'s Y-origin sequence (opacity/blend row `y=132`) puts this as the FIRST content row below the tab bar, no section header text above it. |
| 2 | **Align** | `SingleNodeAlignRow.tsx` (already a separate file, currently mounted as Row 1 of `PositionSection.tsx`) | `alignSelf`, `justifySelf` (or parent `justifyContent` inline, via `resolveAlignWrite.ts`, unchanged) | Penpot shows this as its own dedicated top area, not folded into Measures or Layout — `01-fixtures.md`/screenshots confirm a standalone align/distribute row. |
| 3 | **Measures** | `PositionSection.tsx` (minus Align, minus PositionSwitcher's parent-relationship rows — see Decisions) + `SizeSection.tsx` (W/H) + `AppearanceSection.tsx`'s radius `ExpandableFieldCluster` + `RotationRow.tsx` + `ZIndexSettingsRow.tsx` + `PositionConstraints.tsx`/`ConstraintsDiagram.tsx` | `width`,`height`,`min*`,`max*`,`aspectRatio`,`boxSizing`,`position`,`top`,`right`,`bottom`,`left`,`rotate`,`scale`,`zIndex`, all 4 `border*Radius` | **`02-measurements.md`'s own Y-origins prove radius sits in the SAME section as W/H/X/Y/rotation** (`W/H y=180`, `X/Y y=216 (Δ4)`, `rotation/radius y=252 (Δ4)`) — NOT bundled with opacity/blend as `AppearanceSection.tsx` currently does. This is the single most load-bearing geometry finding in this design: it directly contradicts the current file's grouping and is not optional to apply. `03-operating-behaviors.md`'s CONSTRAINTS-vs-FLEX-ELEMENT structural swap (see Decisions) lives here, not in Layout. |

Good second pick to "prove the pattern" if the team wants a second easy win before Measures/Layout. |

The LAST section to migrate: once this PR lands, `classStyleSections.ts`, `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx`, `StyleSectionsComposer.tsx`, and the `'styles'` manifest entry are ALL deleted in the same PR — nothing from the old registry survives past this point. |

**Margin's fate (Decisions):** Penpot has no CSS-margin concept at all (its shapes are absolutely positioned; there is nothing in `01-fixtures.md`/`02-measurements.md`/screenshots resembling a margin control). Rather than exiling `marginTop/Right/Bottom/Left` to the Studio-extras bucket, this design folds margin into **Layout (item 4)**, directly below the padding cluster it already visually neighbors in `LayoutSection.tsx` today (`classStyleSections.ts`'s own comment: "Padding lives in the Layout cluster now... Margin stays in Spacing... a relationship with siblings") — same box-model mental model, smaller cognitive jump for a user than hunting for it in extras. `SpacingSection.tsx`/`SpacingBoxControl.tsx` are deleted when Layout (item 4) migrates, not held back for item 11.

#### Decisions (the ambiguous calls this design makes explicitly, so a later agent doesn't silently reverse them)

- **Radius moves from Appearance to Measures, opacity+blend stay and become Layer.** Directly required by `02-measurements.md`'s measured Y-origins — not a style preference, a measured fact about where Penpot actually puts these three properties relative to each other.
- **The container/element line for Layout vs. Measures:** Layout (item 4) owns only the flex/grid CONTAINER's own settings (direction/wrap/align/justify/gap/padding/margin/grid tracks/clip). Measures (item 3) owns the ELEMENT's own sizing/position facts, including `03-operating-behaviors.md`'s CONSTRAINTS-vs-FLEX-ELEMENT structural swap: when the selected node's PARENT is not a flex/grid layout, Measures shows Constraints (`PositionConstraints.tsx`/`ConstraintsDiagram.tsx`, left/top anchor + "fix when scrolling"); the moment the parent IS a flex/grid layout, Measures shows the FLEX ELEMENT face instead (Static/Absolute toggle, hug/fill-equivalent sizing buttons reusing `SizeSection.tsx`'s existing `elementSizing.ts` resolution, `ZIndexSettingsRow.tsx`) — **the section changes identity structurally, per Penpot's own confirmed behavior ("the panel never shows both... and never shows a disabled/grayed version of the one that doesn't apply")**, not a mode toggle the user picks. Reuse `LayoutSection/layoutMode.ts`'s existing "is this node's parent a flex/grid container" check for the gate — do not write a second one.
- **The CSS `visibility` toggle (currently `AppearanceSectionActions`' eye, writes `visibility:hidden`, keeps box in flow) is DISTINCT from the new Layer section's structural hide (`toggleNodeHidden`, removes the node from the page).** Both are kept, both stay reachable, but Penpot models only the structural one. This design puts the structural toggle as Layer's PRIMARY eye icon (matching Penpot's real semantics and icon position) and keeps the CSS `visibility:hidden` toggle as a SECONDARY control in the same row (rule 3 — "rare options live in a popover on the field they modify"), tooltipped distinctly exactly as `AppearanceSection.tsx`'s own doc comment already insists the two "hides" must never be confused. Do not drop either.
- **Interaction (`cursor`/`pointerEvents`/`userSelect`/`scrollBehavior`), Animations (`animation*`/`transition*`+keyframes), and the transform/transformOrigin raw-text popover all fold into Studio extras (item 11).** None of the three has a Penpot equivalent (Penpot's own "Prototype" tab covers screen-to-screen interaction, a completely different concept from CSS `cursor`/`transition`) — `classStyleSections.ts`'s own pre-existing comment already says as much for Interaction ("Figma has no CSS-cursor/pointer-events concept... so both stay at the end"), and the same reasoning applies unchanged to Penpot. This is the one point where this design fills a real gap in the plan's own 6-word gloss for item 11 ("Component props (call-site), Attributes, Custom properties") — the plan's prose undercounts what item 11 actually has to absorb; flagging explicitly rather than leaving Interaction/Animations/transform stranded with no destination.
- **The node's `label`/name stays where P1 already put it** (`NodeHeader.tsx`, rendered in `PanelHeader`'s persistent `titleContent`, ABOVE the Design/Prototype/Inspect tab strip — confirmed by reading `PropertiesPanel.tsx`/`InspectorShell.tsx`). P0 never measured a distinct "name row" inside Penpot's Design-tab BODY separate from panel chrome, so there is no measured contradiction forcing a move, and moving it would mean re-touching `PropertiesPanel.tsx`'s header wiring that P1 already built and works. The Layer section (item 1) therefore does NOT re-render the name — it starts directly with visibility/lock/opacity/blend.
- **`toggleNodeLocked` has ZERO existing UI call sites anywhere in the admin today** (grepped: only `nodeActions.ts`/`types.ts` reference it; `toggleNodeHidden` has a real call site in `LayerNodeContextMenu.tsx`, `toggleNodeLocked` has none). Layer's lock icon is the FIRST real UI for this store action, not a re-skin of an existing control — budget it as new UI work, not a port. `pixel-art-icons` has `lock-solid` but no unlock/unlocked variant — follow `panel-22`'s own precedent for `flexWrap`'s missing wrap glyph exactly: hand-draw the missing unlocked-state glyph in `@ui/components/InspectorIcons`, do not invent a second icon-sourcing mechanism.

#### Section 1 template — Layer (concrete enough to implement directly)

**New files:**
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/LayerSection.tsx`
- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/LayerSection.module.css`

**Deletes (this section's own PR):**
- `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/AppearanceSection.tsx` + `.module.css` — but ONLY once Measures (item 3) has also taken the radius half; if Layer lands before Measures, temporarily keep `AppearanceSection.tsx`'s radius-only remainder alive (strip its opacity/blend/eye/droplet code, leave the `ExpandableFieldCluster` body) rather than leaving two components racing to write `opacity`. Sequence Layer before Measures or Measures before Layer, never land one without immediately following with the other — they are the ONE old file this design splits across two new sections, everything else maps one-old-file(s)-to-one-new-section cleanly.
- `classStyleSections.ts`'s `appearance` entry — split: `opacity`/`mixBlendMode`/`visibility` move to Layer's own claim (or, if `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` is being kept alive as a shared registry until item 11's PR — see the mapping table's own note that the file survives until then — leave a `layer`-id entry there with just those three properties, purely for the "N set"/search bookkeeping other code may still read; if nothing reads it once P1's search bar is gone, confirm with a grep before assuming it must be kept), `border*Radius` moves to Measures.

**Component shape:**

```tsx
// src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/LayerSection.tsx
import { useEditorStore } from '@site/store/store'
import { useEditorPermissions } from '@site/editorPermissionsContext'
import { useSelectionModel } from '../selectionModel'
import { useInspectorCommit } from '../commitApi'
import { ScrubInput } from '@ui/components/ScrubInput'
import { Button } from '@ui/components/Button'
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuSeparator } from '@ui/components/ContextMenu'
import { EyeSolidIcon } from 'pixel-art-icons/icons/eye-solid'
import { EyeOffSolidIcon } from 'pixel-art-icons/icons/eye-off-solid'
import { LockSolidIcon } from 'pixel-art-icons/icons/lock-solid'
import { UnlockedIcon } from '@ui/components/InspectorIcons' // NEW hand-drawn glyph, see Decisions
import { ColorsSwatchSolidIcon } from 'pixel-art-icons/icons/colors-swatch-solid'
import { readString, hasStyleValue, plainString } from '../../panels/PropertiesPanel/styleValueUtils'
// ... blend-mode groups/label ported VERBATIM from AppearanceSection.tsx (BLEND_MODE_GROUPS, blendModeLabel) — do not rewrite, move.
import styles from './LayerSection.module.css'

export function LayerSection() {
  const model = useSelectionModel()
  const commit = useInspectorCommit(model)
  const toggleNodeHidden = useEditorStore((s) => s.toggleNodeHidden)
  const toggleNodeLocked = useEditorStore((s) => s.toggleNodeLocked)
  const canEditStructure = useEditorPermissions().canEditStructure
  const { selectedNodeId, selectedNode } = model
  if (!selectedNodeId || !selectedNode) return null

  const isHidden = selectedNode.hidden === true          // structural — Penpot's real eye semantics
  const isLocked = selectedNode.locked === true            // ZERO prior UI — new surface, see Decisions
  const isCssHidden = readString(selectedNode.inlineStyles ?? {}, 'visibility') === 'hidden' // secondary, Studio-only

  const opacityValue = /* read from model.provenanceByProperty / node bag exactly as AppearanceSection.tsx did, ported not rewritten */
  const blendValue = /* same port */

  return (
    <div className={styles.layerRow} data-testid="inspector-layer-row">
      <Button iconOnly size="xs" variant="ghost" pressed={isHidden}
        aria-label={isHidden ? 'Show on canvas' : 'Hide on canvas'}
        tooltip={isHidden ? 'Show on canvas' : 'Hide on canvas'}
        onClick={() => toggleNodeHidden(selectedNodeId)}>
        {isHidden ? <EyeOffSolidIcon size={14} /> : <EyeSolidIcon size={14} />}
      </Button>
      {canEditStructure && (
        <Button iconOnly size="xs" variant="ghost" pressed={isLocked}
          aria-label={isLocked ? 'Unlock element' : 'Lock element'}
          tooltip={isLocked ? 'Unlock element' : 'Lock element'}
          onClick={() => toggleNodeLocked(selectedNodeId)}>
          {isLocked ? <LockSolidIcon size={14} /> : <UnlockedIcon size={14} />}
        </Button>
      )}
      <ScrubInput fieldSize="sm" label="%" value={opacityValue} unit="%" min={0} max={100}
        aria-label="Opacity"
        onChange={(v) => commit.commitStyle('opacity', v || null)}
        onPreview={(v) => commit.commitStyle('opacity', v || null, { preview: true })}
        onClearPreview={commit.clearStylePreview} />
      {/* Blend-mode trigger + ContextMenu — ported VERBATIM from AppearanceSectionActions, calling commit.commitStyle('mixBlendMode', ...) instead of the old onChange prop */}
      {/* Secondary CSS-visibility toggle — a smaller, visually de-emphasized icon in the same row (rule 3), calling commit.commitStyle('visibility', isCssHidden ? null : 'hidden') */}
    </div>
  )
}
```

Geometry: row height `32px` (`--inspector-row-h`), no section header/title text (per the Y-origin finding — this is the very first content row, unlabeled), field gaps use the new `--inspector-gap-tight` (`4px`) between the icon buttons and `--inspector-gap-group` is not needed within this one row. Register in the manifest:

```ts
// sections/index.ts
{ id: 'layer', order: 0, appliesTo: (m) => m.selectedNode != null, Component: LayerSection },
```
(`StyleSectionsComposer`'s existing entry keeps `order: 0` too until it's fully dismantled — bump it as sections peel off, or renumber all entries each PR; either is fine as long as `order` reflects the CURRENT Penpot sequence after that PR lands.)

**Locked-properties notice, ported per this design's own top-level note:** filter `selectedNode.codeProps` for `style:opacity`/`style:mixBlendMode` keys; if either is code-locked, disable that one field (not the whole row) with the same lock icon + tooltip pattern `StyleSectionsComposer.tsx` already uses — do not disable the whole Layer row for one locked property.

**Gate for this section:** a new `layerSection.test.tsx` under `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/__tests__/` asserting: eye toggles `node.hidden` (not `visibility`) and reads back correctly; lock is hidden without `canEditStructure`; opacity commits through `commitApi`'s existing preview channel (assert `previewNodeStyles`/`previewClassStyles` fire, not a direct store write, mid-drag); blend-mode menu writes `mixBlendMode` through `commitStyle`, `undefined` for `'normal'` (port the existing `AppearanceSection` test assertions for this, don't re-derive them).

#### Sections 2-11 — sequencing and per-section verification discipline

Implement in this order (matches the plan's own Penpot frequency-of-use order, already sensible — Layer first because it is genuinely the simplest new build and proves the "no manual collapse, forceOpen, Studio-extras-for-orphans" pattern the same way `live-05`'s Batch 2 was picked specifically because it was low-risk):

1. Layer (full template above)
2. Measures (must follow Layer immediately — see the `AppearanceSection.tsx` split note above)
3. Align
4. Layout
5. Stroke (flagged above as the next-lowest-risk pick — do this before Fill if the team wants a second easy win)
6. Fill
7. Shadow
8. Blur (must follow Shadow immediately — both share `EffectsSection.tsx`, whose deletion is gated on both landing)
9. Text
10. Export (can move earlier in this order if desired — it is nearly free after Step 0's token change; not a dependency for anything else, purely a scheduling convenience)
11. Studio extras (last, by construction — deletes `classStyleSections.ts`/`StyleSectionsEditor.tsx`/`StyleSectionsComposer.tsx` and the old `'styles'` manifest entry)

**For sections 2-11, this design intentionally does NOT paste field-by-field JSX the way Layer's template does** — each old source file is already named per-section in the mapping table above, and each is different enough (Measures needs the CONSTRAINTS/FLEX-ELEMENT structural swap; Layout needs the container/element line drawn; Fill/Stroke are largely geometry re-skins of already-close code; Text is the closest to done) that pre-writing their JSX here would either be wrong in a way nobody catches until implementation, or would balloon this entry past the point of being readable. **Read the named old file(s) in full immediately before starting that section's own PR** (the same discipline `live-05`'s Batch 5 note establishes: "if it's bigger than expected, split it into its own follow-up rather than block the rest"). Each section's own PR must independently:
  - Re-read its slice of `02-measurements.md`/`03-operating-behaviors.md`/the relevant fixture screenshot before writing geometry, not rely on this entry's summary table alone.
  - Build its section as its own manifest entry with a real `appliesTo` (e.g., Text: `(m) => isTextNode(m.selectedNode)`, reusing `styleSectionOrder.ts`'s existing `isTextNode` — do not duplicate that check).
  - Pass `forceOpen` to `Section` (or build lighter custom chrome if `Section`'s toggle-suppression doesn't fit — Penpot's own section header IS a plain uppercase label + trailing icons, `02-measurements.md`'s "Section headers" table, so `Section`'s icon-marker-doubles-as-chevron design may not even be the right primitive; evaluate per section, don't assume `Section` is reused unchanged everywhere the way Layer's template does — Layer has NO header at all, most of the other 10 DO have a Penpot uppercase header and should keep using `Section` with `forceOpen`).
  - Reuse every pure value-logic file named in the mapping table verbatim (`fillModel.ts`, `backgroundLayers.ts`, `boxShadowLayers.ts`, `elementSizing.ts`, `resolveAlignWrite.ts`, etc.) — none of these need to change; only the RENDERING components around them do.
  - Delete its own old file(s) in the SAME PR, per the plan's "each deletes its predecessor" rule — never leave an old and new section rendering side by side, and never defer a deletion to "P3 cleanup at the end."
  - Shrink `classStyleSections.ts`'s `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` array by removing whichever entries just migrated (or their claimed-properties subset, where a category splits across two new sections — Layer/Measures, Shadow/Blur).
  - Run `bun run build && bun test && bun run lint` before considering that section's PR done — the plan's own text requires each PR leave the tree building, not just the final one.

#### Contracts

`InspectorSectionDefinition`/`SelectionModel`/`InspectorCommitApi` are UNCHANGED from `panel-23` — paste is unnecessary, read that entry's own Contracts block. The only NEW shape this design introduces is the `LayerSection`/per-section component pattern shown above, which every other section's own component should structurally mirror (reads `useSelectionModel()`+`useInspectorCommit(model)`, takes no props, returns `null` on no selection, is registered in `sections/index.ts` with a real `appliesTo`).

#### Gates

- `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/__tests__/layerSection.test.tsx` (new, section 1) — see Layer's own gate note above.
- Each subsequent section gets its own `<name>Section.test.tsx` under the same `__tests__/` folder, porting (not re-deriving) the OLD section's existing test assertions from `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/__tests__/<oldName>.test.tsx` onto the new component — the old test files get deleted alongside their component, per the same "no old and new side by side" rule.
- `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/__tests__/emptySectionLaw.test.tsx` and `inspectorGeometryBudget.test.tsx` reference `StyleSectionsEditor`/`CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` directly — both need updating EVERY time a section migrates out (their assertions about which sections are `collapsedWhenEmpty` and their `FROZEN_INSPECTOR_TOKENS` table both shrink/change per section), and get deleted outright in item 11's PR when their subject file is deleted. `inspectorGeometryBudget.test.tsx`'s own `FROZEN_INSPECTOR_TOKENS` table needs its `row-h`/`pad-x`/`field-radius` rows updated to `32px`/`12px`/`8px` as part of Step 0, immediately — this is a live, currently-passing assertion against the OLD wrong numbers that Step 0's token change will otherwise silently break.
- No NEW architecture gate is required by this pass — P4's `no-full-site-scan-in-selectors.test.ts` extension already covers every new section (they all read through `useSelectionModel`, which that gate is scoped to). The eventual full-registry deletion (`StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` et al.) is P6's gate (`src/__tests__/inspector/measurement.test.ts`, not yet written) — do not build that gate now; P6 owns it, once ALL 11 sections have landed.
- `module-size-budgets.test.ts` — several old files this design pulls apart (`PositionSection.tsx`, `EffectsSection.tsx`) are already split across sibling files for exactly this budget; the new per-section files should stay under the same ceiling, watch it per-PR rather than assume it holds.

#### Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Landing Layer without Measures (or vice versa) leaves `AppearanceSection.tsx` half-deleted and two components both able to write `opacity`/radius | Sequence them back-to-back, never separately verified-green in between (this design's only exception to "each section is independently gated green") |
| A section's re-skin silently drops a property from `classStyleSections.ts`'s claim list, making it invisible to whatever still reads "N set" counts | Grep for `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` consumers before each section's properties move — confirm nothing besides the (soon fully retired) search/count machinery still needs the claim, and if something does, keep a claim entry until item 11 removes the whole file |
| The 46-file `--inspector-space-*` blast radius gets touched piecemeal and drifts into a half-4px/half-16px/half-old-scale mess across sections migrated at different times | Only ever use the two NEW tokens in NEW section files; never edit an old, not-yet-migrated file's `.module.css` space usage as a "quick fix" mid-pass |
| `toggleNodeLocked`'s total lack of prior UI means its first real exercise is inside a brand-new component with no existing test to port from | Layer's own gate (above) is written from scratch specifically because there is no old test to port — budget real time for this one section's tests, unlike sections 2-11 which mostly port existing assertions |

**Built independently of Layer (PR #101), by design, not by accident.** Checked first whether Align's own design needs Layer's actual diff: Align pulls from `SingleNodeAlignRow.tsx`/`resolveAlignWrite.ts`, which touch neither `AppearanceSection.tsx` nor `opacity`/`mixBlendMode` — zero file overlap with Layer's PR. Only the shared PATTERN (manifest entry shape, `useSelectionModel()`/`useInspectorCommit()`, `MIGRATED_SECTION_PROPERTIES`-style reasoning) was needed, and that was fully readable from this entry's own template + Layer's committed diff on `origin/feat/inspector-section-layer` without merging it. **Did not merge Layer into this worktree** — confirmed `bun run build`/`bun test` green on top of plain `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` alone. The one real cost of building the two in parallel: `sections/index.ts`'s `order` numbering. This PR adds `{ id: 'align', order: 0 }` and bumps `styles` to `order: 1` — the exact same convention Layer's PR used for its own `{ id: 'layer', order: 0 }` — so when both PRs land, whoever merges second will hit a real (expected, trivial) conflict on that one array and must renumber to `layer: 0, align: 1, styles: 2`. Flagging explicitly so it isn't mistaken for a bug.

**A real, P0-evidenced design correction over the old `SingleNodeAlignRow`, not just a location move:** the old component always rendered all 6 align buttons, fully disabled with a reason tooltip, whenever the selection had no flex/grid parent. Re-checked against the P0 screenshots per this entry's own instruction to verify geometry against the actual fixture, not just the summary table (there is no `02-measurements.md` row for Align at all — none of the 4 fixtures needed it) — `docs/audits/penpot-inspector-baseline/screenshots/f1-rectangle/dark/design.png` (bare rectangle, no layout parent) shows NO align row at all, only the boolean-ops icon row; `f3-flexboard/dark/design-child.png` (a rectangle that IS a flex child) shows the align row as the panel's very first content row. Penpot's align row does not exist in the DOM when nothing on it could ever write anything — it isn't a permanently-resident, sometimes-disabled control. `AlignSection.tsx` now matches this: it computes `resolveAlignWrite` for all 6 edges and returns `null` when every one comes back `unavailable` (no parent / no live frame / non-flex-grid parent), rather than rendering a fully-disabled row. A PARTIAL disable (e.g. a flex main-axis edge refused because of siblings while the cross axis stays honest) still renders normally — only the "nothing here would ever work" case hides the whole row. This directly matches rule 2 ("nothing rendered that lies") better than the pre-existing component did; noting it as a deliberate, evidenced divergence from a literal 1:1 port, per this work order's own instruction to re-verify each section's geometry independently rather than trust the summary table alone.

**The Constraints-vs-Flex-element identity swap — implemented as the ONE concrete difference P0 actually evidenced, not a guess at Penpot's unstated internals.** Re-checked both fixture screenshots directly (not just `03-operating-behaviors.md`'s prose) before writing this: `screenshots/f1-rectangle/dark/design.png` (a bare rectangle with NO parent frame at all) shows the W/H/X/Y/rotation/radius block with no header, going straight to a collapsed LAYOUT section afterward — no CONSTRAINTS section is visible at all for this fixture, which is a real gap against `03-operating-behaviors.md`'s own prose claim that "a shape with no layout parent... shows a CONSTRAINTS section" (P0 never screenshotted that exact case — a plain BOARD's non-flex child — per `01-fixtures.md`'s own "what's deliberately not a fixture" note; the only "no parent" case actually captured is the page-root rectangle, which shows no such section). `screenshots/f3-flexboard/dark/design-child.png` (a rectangle that IS a flex child) DOES show a real, screenshotted uppercase "FLEX ELEMENT" header, containing a Static/Absolute toggle, icon-only sizing buttons, and a "Z --" field. Given this asymmetry in what P0 actually evidenced (a real header shape for the flex case, no evidenced header shape at all for the non-flex case, and no decoded CSS semantics for the FLEX ELEMENT icon row's exact buttons), `MeasuresSection` implements the identity swap as a header-label difference ONLY: the existing position switcher + direction-inputs/constraints content (already ported from `PositionSection.tsx`, unchanged) renders unwrapped and unlabeled when the parent is NOT flex/grid, and wrapped in a `forceOpen` `Section` titled "Flex element" when it IS — gated by `LayoutSection/layoutMode.ts`'s existing `resolveLayoutMode` check fed the PARENT's computed `display`/`flexDirection` (reused via `useSizingParentLayout()`, not re-derived, per this entry's own explicit instruction).

**Three deliberate divergences from a literal per-pixel Penpot mirror, each documented in `MeasuresSection.tsx`'s own doc header (same posture `AlignSection`'s "hides entirely" divergence took):**
1. **Z-index stays resident regardless of face.** Penpot's plain-rectangle screenshot shows no Z field at all; its FLEX ELEMENT header shows one. Studio's `zIndex` is a generically useful CSS escape hatch with no flex/grid dependency (e.g. two absolutely-positioned siblings with no shared layout) — gating it behind "is the parent flex/grid" would be a real feature loss for a fact orthogonal to what the property does, not a faithful port. It moved off its old rotation-paired row (now occupied by radius) onto the position/constraints row instead, in BOTH faces.
2. **No new Static/Absolute toggle or icon-button hug/fill control were built.** Studio's existing `position` `DropdownSwitcher` already encodes exactly the Static(in-flow)/Absolute distinction Penpot's toggle would express, and `SizeSection`'s existing Fixed/Hug/Fill picker already disables Hug/Fill with a named reason whenever `useSizingParentLayout` reports no real parent layout (the honest substance behind Penpot's FLEX ELEMENT sizing buttons) — inventing a second, parallel control for either would be UI that lies about a CSS distinction Studio's model doesn't separately have.
3. **The Constraints face's CONTENT (position switcher + TRBL grid or `PositionConstraints`) is identical to the Flex-element face's content** — only the header label differs, per the evidence gap above.

#### Done so far — Section 5 (Fill), 2026-09-14

**PR #110 (draft), branch `feat/inspector-section-fill`, cut from `origin/feat/alm-figma-killer-studio-shell` with `origin/feat/inspector-section-layer` (#101), `origin/feat/inspector-section-align` (#105), `origin/feat/inspector-section-measures` (#107), and `origin/feat/inspector-section-layout` (#108) merged in FIRST, in that order.** Worktree `.tmp/wt-panel-25-fill` (now removable). Scope: Section 5 (Fill) ONLY. Merges: Layer clean; Align conflicted in `sections/index.ts` (both independently added `order: 0` entries — resolved to `layer: 0, align: 1, styles: 2`); Measures conflicted the same way (resolved to `layer: 0, align: 1, measures: 2, styles: 3`); Layout merged CLEAN (auto-resolved the manifest array to `layer: 0, align: 1, measures: 2, layout: 3, styles: 4`) — confirmed `bun run build` clean after each merge step, before writing any of this PR's own code, per this work order's own discipline.

**Old `FillSection.tsx`'s own mount condition, checked rather than guessed:** it had no `appliesTo`-equivalent gate at all in `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` — `classStyleSections.ts`'s `fill` entry rendered for any selected node via the generic section-list iteration. `sections/index.ts`'s new `fill` entry mirrors this exactly: `appliesTo: (m) => m.selectedNode != null`, same predicate every migrated section (Layer/Align/Measures/Layout) already uses — no node kind was ever excluded from Fill.

**The Color field chrome — `02-measurements.md`'s key finding for this section, implemented as a genuinely NEW inline control, not a re-skin.** The old `FillSection.tsx` showed a fill/solid-colour value only via `PropertyList`'s `summary` text (a hex string), requiring a click into a popover to see or touch anything else about it — no opacity was visible or editable at the row level at all. Penpot's own measured chrome is one flat row: swatch → hex → `%` opacity → remove. Rather than rewriting `PropertyList`'s shared interaction model (used identically by Stroke/Effects, well outside this PR's scope) to make the hex field itself inline-editable, this design adds a genuinely NEW `ColorOpacityField` (`FillSectionParts.tsx`) into `PropertyList`'s existing `value` slot — a slot whose own doc comment already names "an opacity %" as its intended use, so this is filling a documented gap, not inventing a new primitive shape. It reads/writes the alpha channel of the SAME colour value via `parseCssColor`/`formatColor` (`@ui/components/ColorPickerPopover` — an existing, already-tested pure colour model built for `ColorPickerPopover`'s own alpha rail, reused here rather than inventing a second alpha-channel implementation) — CSS has no separate "fill opacity" property the way Penpot's own object model does, so the alpha channel already inside `#rrggbbaa`/`rgba(...)`/`hsla(...)` IS that number. A value the parser cannot decompose (a `var(--token)` reference, `currentColor`, an unrecognised colour function) disables the field rather than guessing an alpha — the same "never a guessed rewrite" rule the layer-stack parser and the gradient parser already follow. Only the Text and Solid-fill entries get this field — a gradient layer's per-stop colours already carry their own alpha inside `GradientEditor`, and an image layer has no colour at all.

**Law 1 / Rule 2, implemented locally, not through the (now-partially-dismantled) shared `StyleSectionsEditor`/`StyleSectionGroup` machinery.** `classStyleSections.ts`'s `fill` entry is gone, so there is no `collapsedWhenEmpty` flag or `revealedSectionIds` local state to inherit anymore — `FillSection.tsx` computes its own `setAnywhere` (set on the active context OR any breakpoint/condition override, mirroring `StyleSectionsComposer.tsx`'s own `crossContextStyles` construction) and renders `Section`'s `empty` prop directly when nothing is set (title + add buttons, no chevron — matches Penpot's own measured collapsed-empty convention, and matches the OLD Fill section's pre-existing Law-1 behaviour exactly) or `forceOpen` when anything is (no manual collapse of a populated section — Rule 2, the same posture Layer/Align/Measures already established). No `revealed`-style local UI state was needed: every header "+" button (`FillSectionActions`, moved unchanged) already writes a REAL value immediately on click (`onChange('color', DEFAULT_TEXT_FILL)`, etc.) rather than merely revealing an empty body, so the write itself is what flips `Section` from empty to populated on the very next render — simpler than the old `StyleSectionsEditor`'s two-step reveal-then-write dance for OTHER (non-Fill) sections.

**Multi-select simplification, following Align's own already-established fact.** The old `FillSection.tsx` carried `isMixed`/`MIXED_PLACEHOLDER` handling for `MultiInlineStyleComposer`'s multi-node case. The new manifest section is structurally unreachable during multi-select (`PropertiesPanelBody.tsx` renders `MultiSelectionInspector` before `StyleSurface`/`INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` ever mount — the same fact `AlignSection.tsx`'s own doc already relies on), so all of that handling was dropped rather than ported as dead code.

**How the node-level (non-`StyleRule`-shaped) contract wiring actually worked out — read this before the next node-level section.** The dispatch predicted `ExportSection`'s "internal read/write plumbing may look different" from every prior section, and it was right in two specific ways:
1. **No `useInspectorCommit(model)` call at all.** Every section in items 1-9 calls it because every one of them WRITES a CSS property through `commitStyle`/`commitStyleMany`. Export writes nothing to the node (a file download, two clipboard copies, a server JSX read) — there is no commit API surface for it to use. `ExportSection()` calls only `useSelectionModel()` plus two of its own narrow `useEditorStore` selectors (`activePageId`, and the identical `isStudioPageRootId(selectActiveCanvasPage(s)?.rootNodeId)` boolean `SelectionModel`'s own internals already compute privately) — duplicated on purpose rather than widening `SelectionModel`'s public shape for this one, node-level consumer, the same posture `AlignSection.tsx` already established for its own extra `selectActiveCanvasPage` read.
2. **A private, keyed sub-component was required to preserve real behaviour.** The pre-migration mount was `<ExportSection key={nodeId} .../>` — the row list is deliberately unpersisted, per-node session state (`ExportSection.tsx`'s own "Rows are session state" doc, unchanged), so it MUST reset when the selection moves to a different node. But the manifest's shared mount loop (`StyleSurface.tsx`) keys every entry by a CONSTANT `section.id` (`key={section.id}`), never by node — a fact every prior section could ignore because none of them held onto per-node local component state the way Export's row list does. Splitting into `ExportSection()` (the props-less, `null`-on-no-selection manifest entry) rendering `<ExportSectionBody key={nodeId} .../>` (a private, props-driven component that owns the actual `useState` row list) reproduces the old remount-on-selection-change behaviour without touching the shared mount loop. Verified directly: `exportSection.test.tsx`'s "rows reset on selection change" test adds a row, switches `selectedNodeId` via `act(() => selectStudioNode(OTHER_NODE_ID))` + `rerender`, and confirms the row is gone.

**The Rule-2 gap this section closes, found during migration.** The pre-migration file's empty-state branch used `defaultOpen={false}` + `children={null}` (not `Section`'s `empty` prop) and its populated-state branch used `defaultOpen` (not `forceOpen`) — both left a real, hoverable, clickable collapse chevron, on BOTH the empty state (toggling it revealed an empty body) and the populated state (toggling it could hide a real "N ready" export list). Fixed to `Section`'s `empty`/`forceOpen` pair, the same primitive Fill/Shadow/Stroke already use for their own Law-1/Rule-2 compliance — this is a live bug fix, not a redesign; the empty-state markup, PropertyList rows, and all four verbs are otherwise byte-for-byte the same logic.

**Disclosed, deliberate behaviour change — flagged for a human call, not silently applied.** The pre-migration mount rendered Export unconditionally (once node/page/Studio-session were present) regardless of `StyleSurface.tsx`'s own `canEditStyleHere`/`nothingWritable` gates — a read-only-role user, or a structurally-locked node with no writable class, could still export PNG/SVG or copy CSS/JSX. Registering Export as an ordinary `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` entry means it now renders through the SAME shared `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS.filter(appliesTo).sort(order).map(Component)` loop as every CSS-property section, which is gated behind `canEditStyleHere`/`!nothingWritable` in `StyleSurface.tsx`'s own ternary — so Export is now HIDDEN in those two states, same as Layer/Align/Measures/etc. This was not an oversight: pulling Export out of that shared loop to preserve independent visibility would have meant either (a) touching `StyleSurface.tsx`'s render-tree structure beyond "grow the manifest array" (a rule every section since Layer has held to), or (b) rendering it in the wrong visual position relative to `styles` (Penpot order requires Export BEFORE the Studio-extras/`styles` composer, and the old unconditional-bottom-of-column mount already put it AFTER `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` in the render tree — so replicating the old unconditional visibility would have meant a NEW ordering bug, not a neutral preservation). Weighed both ways in `docs/features/inspector-disclosure.md` §G11 and here; a follow-up (a `gatedByWritability: boolean` field on `InspectorSectionDefinition`, or an explicit second, ungated mount slot in `StyleSurface.tsx`) would be the way to restore the old independence if a human decides the read-only/locked-node export capability matters enough to re-add.

This work order does not re-litigate those decisions (Interaction/Animations/transform belong in Studio extras, not the Prototype tab, despite the plan's own literal §P3 item-11 gloss) — it only turns them into files.

##### Decision 1 — ONE manifest section, or several? → **SIX manifest entries, not one "Studio extras" component**

`INSPECTOR_SECTIONS`' 11-numbered plan items already do NOT map 1:1 to manifest entries — items 7/8 (Shadow/Blur) are two separate entries (`shadow`, `blur`) that split out of the same old file in ONE PR. That precedent, plus three facts specific to this item, settle it:

1. The five concerns have genuinely different `appliesTo` predicates (Component only applies to `studio.instance` nodes; the other four apply to any node) — cramming them behind one component's internal `if` ladder reintroduces the per-node-kind branching P1/P3 have spent nine sections removing.
2. They were already FIVE separate headers in the pre-P3 world (`CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` currently has 3 entries — `transform`/`animations`/`interaction` — each its own `Section` header; Attributes and Component were already two more, entirely separate top-level surfaces). One combined section would be a NEW visual grouping Penpot never asked for and the old registry never had either.
3. The Animations cluster alone alone is ~930 lines across its rendering files (`AnimationsSection.tsx` 404 + `AnimationEditorPopover.tsx` 427 + `AnimationScrubRow.tsx` 103) before any adapter glue — combining it into one file with Component/Attributes/Custom-properties/Interaction/Transform would blow past the 700-line `module-size-budgets.test.ts` `CEILING` on day one.

Six new `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` entries, ids and order (contiguous tail block, `export` stays `order: 9`):

| order | id | Component | `appliesTo` | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | `component` | `ComponentSection.tsx` (renamed from `InstanceCallSiteView.tsx`) | `(m) => m.selectedNode?.moduleId === 'studio.instance'` | call-site props |
| 11 | `attributes` | `AttributesSection.tsx` (renamed from `HtmlAttributesPanel.tsx`) | `(m) => m.selectedNode != null` | `htmlAttributes` prop |
| 12 | `transform` | `TransformSection.tsx` (new, ~40 lines) | `(m) => m.selectedNode != null` | `transform`, `transformOrigin` |
| 13 | `animations` | `AnimationsSection.tsx` (new; NOT the same file as the old one of the same name) | `(m) => m.selectedNode != null` | `animation*`, `transition` |
| 14 | `interaction` | `InteractionSection.tsx` (new; NOT the same file as the old one of the same name) | `(m) => m.selectedNode != null` | `cursor`, `pointerEvents`, `userSelect`, `scrollBehavior` |
| 15 | `customProperties` | `CustomPropertiesSection.tsx` (thin new wrapper, NOT the same file as the old one of the same name) | `(m) => m.selectedNode != null` | every uncurated key (`!isCuratedProperty`) |

Order mirrors the pre-migration registry's own relative order where one already existed (`classStyleSections.ts`'s array is literally `transform, animations, interaction` today) plus the plan's own literal item-11 ordering ("Component props, Attributes, Custom properties") for the two node-level concerns that never had an order relative to the CSS-category three. `customProperties` stays last, exactly as it is today (`StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` always renders it after every curated section). The `'styles'` manifest entry (`StyleSectionsComposer`, currently `order: 10`) is deleted outright, not renumbered into this range.

**Not migrated into the manifest at all — stays exactly where it is:** `ComponentParamsOverview.tsx`. Despite row 11 naming it, it renders in a state (`selectedNode === null`, empty-VC-canvas) that `PropertiesPanelBody.tsx` resolves and returns from BEFORE `StyleSurface`/`INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` ever mount (`if (!selectedNode || !definition) { … return <ComponentParamsOverview vc={activeVc} /> }`) — every one of the ten existing manifest entries and all six new ones assume a selected node; inventing a `selectedNode == null` `appliesTo` branch for exactly one entry, or restructuring `PropertiesPanelBody`'s branch router to reach `StyleSurface` in that state, is out of scope (`StyleSurface.tsx`'s mount loop is explicitly never to be touched, and `PropertiesPanelBody`'s branch router sits a level above that). Read row 11's listing of this file as "this concern has no better conceptual home than Studio-extras," not as "this file must physically relocate." **Zero changes to this file or its test (`src/__tests__/editor/ComponentParamsOverview.test.tsx`, renders the bare component with a `vc` prop — untouched).**

##### Decision 2 — `classStyleSections.ts` and `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` do NOT both die in this PR — correcting this entry's own earlier text

Prior "Done so far" notes (Text's own, in particular) assumed item 11 deletes `classStyleSections.ts`/`StyleSectionsEditor.tsx`/`StyleSectionsComposer.tsx` "wholesale." Verified against the actual tree, not assumed: **`classStyleSections.ts` cannot be deleted** — `StyleCategoryRail.tsx` imports `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS`/`orderStyleSections` directly (its rail-button list), and `cssControlTypes.ts` imports `MIGRATED_SECTION_PROPERTIES`/`CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` for `ALL_CURATED_CSS_PROPERTIES`/`isCuratedProperty` — both real, live, out-of-scope-to-redesign consumers (`StyleCategoryRail.tsx` backs `SelectorInspector.tsx`'s ambient-selector surface, named out of scope as far back as item 9's own entry). What this PR actually does to that file:

- Delete the `transform`/`animations`/`interaction` entries from `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` (leaving it `[]`) — union their full property lists into `MIGRATED_SECTION_PROPERTIES`, the EXACT pattern every one of items 1–9 already used for their own migrated categories (confirmed: Measures/Layout/Fill/Stroke/Text's own "Done so far" notes all did this identically).
- Keep `ClassStyleSectionDefinition`, `getClassStyleSectionSetCounts`, `getActiveStyleTab`, and the now-empty `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` exported — `StyleCategoryRail.tsx`/`StyleRuleComposer.tsx`/`MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx` still import them.
- Update the file's own top-of-file doc comment to state P3 is complete and `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` is permanently `[]`, kept alive only for the two out-of-scope ambient/multi-select surfaces.

**`StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` CAN be deleted, but only after its last two real callers stop needing it.** With `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` at `[]`, `StyleSectionsEditor`'s entire remaining value to its two other callers (`StyleRuleComposer.tsx` — ambient/global-selector; `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx` — multi-select) is rendering `CustomPropertiesSection` — the curated-section loop it also runs is now permanently a no-op. Concretely, in the SAME PR:

- `StyleRuleComposer.tsx`: replace its `<StyleSectionsEditor storedStyles=... currentStyles=... crossContextStyles=... sectionKey=... styleQuery=... onChange=... onRemove=... onClearProperties=... onChangeMany=... onPreview=... onClearPreview=... provenanceByProperty=... styleTarget=... textFirst=... />` call with a direct `<CustomPropertiesSection storedStyles={storedStyles} defaultOpen={sectionsExpanded} onChange={onChange} onRemove={onRemove} />` call. Drop every prop/local computation that fed ONLY that call (`crossContextStyles`, `sectionKey`, `provenanceByProperty`, `styleTarget`, `textFirst`, `onClearProperties`, `onChangeMany`, `onPreview`, `onClearPreview`) **after** grepping the file to confirm each one has no other reader — `handleClearProperty`/`removeClassStyleProperty` were ALREADY dropped from this file during Stroke's own PR (per that entry's own note), so this list may be shorter than it looks. Drop the now-unused `getActiveStyleTab`-driven `sectionKey` if nothing else in the file needs it.
- `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx`: same swap. Its own `isTextSelection(nodes)` call (currently feeding `textFirst`) — grep for any OTHER reader before deleting it; if none, delete it and its now-unused import.
- `StyleRuleComposer.tsx`'s `styleQuery` PROP (accepted from `SelectorInspector.tsx`) has no more consumer once `StyleSectionsEditor`'s search-filter is gone. Drop it from `StyleRuleComposerProps` and delete the one-line `styleQuery={styleQuery}` pass from `SelectorInspector.tsx`'s call site — this is the ONLY line this PR touches in `SelectorInspector.tsx` (see "StyleCategoryRail/SelectorInspector" below for why nothing else there changes).
- Delete `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` and `StyleSectionsComposer.tsx` (the manifest's `'styles'` entry) outright, and the `'styles'` entry from `sections/index.ts`.
- Delete `classStyleSections.ts`'s now-fully-inert `orderStyleSections`/`isTextSelection`/`textFirst` machinery? **No** — `styleSectionOrder.ts` (a separate file) stays: `StyleCategoryRail.tsx`'s own rail-order call and `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx`'s own `isTextSelection` (if still read for anything besides the now-deleted `textFirst` wiring — check) still import it. If the grep in the bullet above shows `isTextSelection` in `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx` has no other reader, its IMPORT there is deleted, but `styleSectionOrder.ts` itself is NOT deleted — `StyleCategoryRail.tsx` still calls `orderStyleSections` on the (now permanently empty) `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS`, which is an inert no-op call, not dead code to remove (removing it would be touching `StyleCategoryRail.tsx`'s own behavior, out of scope — see below).

##### `StyleCategoryRail.tsx` / `SelectorInspector.tsx` — explicit keep/delete guidance

**Zero changes to `StyleCategoryRail.tsx`.** It is not on any deletion list this PR touches (`classStyleSections.ts` stays, exporting everything it imports). Its behavior changes anyway, honestly and by construction, not by an edit: with `CLASS_STYLE_SECTIONS` now `[]`, its "one button per CSS style category" loop renders zero CSS-category buttons — an empty rail below the (always-hidden-in-global-mode) module button, i.e. nothing. This is not new: it has been shrinking one button per section since Layer's own PR; item 11 just finishes it. Filing a follow-up to delete `StyleCategoryRail`'s rendering entirely (an empty rail is worse than no rail) is worth doing but is its own PR — this one does not touch the file.

**One line touched in `SelectorInspector.tsx`:** stop passing `styleQuery={styleQuery}` to `<StyleRuleComposer>` (see above). The `SearchBar` JSX, its `styleQuery` state, and everything else in the file stay untouched. **Disclosed, not silently accepted:** with nothing left behind it to filter (Custom Properties never respected `styleQuery` even before this pass — `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx` hid it entirely whenever a query was non-empty), that search box already typed into empty results for every section 1–9 migrated away; after this PR it types into empty results unconditionally. Recommend a follow-up ticket (fold `SelectorInspector.tsx`'s ambient-selector surface onto `SelectionModel` for real, or delete the dead search chrome) — flagged as a named follow-up per `panel-23`'s own precedent for multi-select, not fixed here.
