### panel-23 — P4: SelectionModel, section manifest, one commit API
- **Agent:** store-engineer (Phase A DONE) + panel-designer (Phase B DONE — see its own subsection below; PR #99 open, draft)
- **Stage:** verifying (PR #99 draft, blocked on #96/#97 landing before it can go ready-for-review — see Phase B's "PR sequencing"). Done-when items (1)-(3) met; item (4) — the two NEW bench budgets (scrub tick, typing latency) — explicitly NOT done this pass, see Phase B's own note.
- **Updated:** 2026-09-13
- **Goal:** `STUDIO-LIVE-CANVAS-PLAN.md` §P4. Replace `usePropertiesPanelData.ts`'s whole-`s.site` subscription — the confirmed, unfixed root cause P1/P2 (`panel-21`/`panel-22`) both explicitly left open for rule 8 (selection→painted-panel ≤16ms) — with one narrow `SelectionModel` selector; introduce a section manifest so P3 can add Penpot-ordered sections without touching the shell's mount logic again; collapse every style/prop write in the single-selection path onto one `commitStyle`/`commitProp` API. **Done when:** (1) `bun run bench` reports selection→paint ≤16ms on the existing 11-section/wide-node fixture panel-22 already built (today it fails — confirmed live by reading `usePropertiesPanelData.ts:106`, `const site = useEditorStore((s) => s.site)`, completely unchanged by P1/P2); (2) `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx` is deleted, not extended — its own doc comment (`panel-21`) already says P4 replaces it wholesale; (3) the extended `no-full-site-scan-in-selectors.test.ts` fails on a reintroduced `useEditorStore((s) => s.site)` (or `state.site`) whole-object selector anywhere under `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/`; (4) two new `bun run bench` budgets exist (scrub tick ≤4ms, typing latency ≤1 frame) — selection→paint's budget already exists (`panel-22`), it just needs to actually pass now.

#### Step 0 — mandatory, before any P4 code: merge P1 + P2 in a fresh worktree, and resolve one REAL semantic conflict

Neither `feat/inspector-shell-p1` (PR #97) nor `feat/inspector-speed-rules-p2` (PR #96) is merged to `origin/main`. Both branch from the identical commit `8ab00ae` (`fix(inspector): fill with an image` (#89) is their shared parent — actually their tip commits are `8594bf4` and `e267537` respectively, both one commit ahead of `8ab00ae`), so there is no base drift to worry about — but **the two branches independently built the SAME feature (P2 rule 7, the inline-style preview channel) with two different, incompatible shapes**, confirmed by diffing both branches against their common base:

- `src/admin/pages/site/store/slices/styleRule/types.ts` and `.../styleRule/uiStateActions.ts` — **both branches add an identical-looking `NodeStylesPreview` type + `setPreviewNodeStyles`/`clearPreviewNodeStyles` pair at the same insertion point, with genuinely different field shapes.** P1's version: `{ nodeId: string; styles: ... }` (singular). P2's version: `{ nodeIds: string[]; styles: ... }` (array — supports `MultiInlineStyleComposer`'s N-node case). This WILL show as a real git conflict, not an auto-mergeable identical patch (`styleRuleSlice.ts`'s own diff IS byte-identical between the two branches and merges silently — only `types.ts`/`uiStateActions.ts` conflict).
- The two branches also built **two different consuming mechanisms** for that same preview state: P1 added `src/admin/pages/site/canvas/NodeStylePreviewInjector.tsx` (a new CSS-injector using `generateNodePreviewCSS` in `canvasClassCss.ts` — the same doubled-`[data-node-id][data-node-id]`-attribute-selector specificity trick `generateForcedStateCSS` already uses), mounted in `IframeFrameSurface.tsx`, and consumed only from `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`'s own `handlePreview`/`handleClearPreview` (`setPreviewNodeStyles({ nodeId, styles: patch })`). P2 instead merges the preview patch **directly into the rendered `style=""` attribute** inside `NodeRenderer.tsx` via a new `mergePreviewedInlineStyles` helper in `canvasNodeInlineStyle.ts`, consumed from `InlineStyleComposer.tsx`/`MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx` (`setPreviewNodeStyles({ nodeIds: [nodeId], styles: patch })` / `setPreviewNodeStyles({ nodeIds: writableNodeIds, styles: patch })`).

**Resolution — keep P2's shape and mechanism, delete P1's:** P1's own `NodeStylePreviewInjector.tsx` doc comment admits the CSS-injector approach "cannot outrank a REAL `style=\"\"` value already present for the same property" — a real, documented limitation P2's direct-merge approach does not have (a direct merge into the node's own `style=""` is definitionally the highest-specificity value there is). P2's `nodeIds: string[]` shape is also the more general one (P1's singular `nodeId` would need widening for multi-select anyway). Concretely, in the merge worktree:
1. Resolve the `types.ts`/`uiStateActions.ts` conflicts by taking P2's `nodeIds: string[]` version verbatim (delete P1's `nodeId`-singular hunks).
2. Delete P1's `src/admin/pages/site/canvas/NodeStylePreviewInjector.tsx` outright, its import + `<NodeStylePreviewInjector ... />` mount (2 lines + a comment) in `IframeFrameSurface.tsx`, and `generateNodePreviewCSS` (+ its test coverage) in `canvasClassCss.ts`.
3. In `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`'s `handlePreview`, change `setPreviewNodeStyles({ nodeId, styles: patch })` to `setPreviewNodeStyles({ nodeIds: [nodeId], styles: patch })` to match the surviving shape — this keeps the file buildable for the short window before Phase A deletes it outright (see below).

**Worktree setup, mirroring `live-05`'s Step 0 pattern:**
```
git fetch origin
git worktree add .tmp/wt-panel-23 -b feat/inspector-selection-model origin/main
cd .tmp/wt-panel-23
git merge origin/feat/inspector-shell-p1
git merge origin/feat/inspector-speed-rules-p2   # will conflict on types.ts + uiStateActions.ts — resolve per the 3 steps above
bun install && bun run build && bun test src/__tests__/panels src/__tests__/architecture   # confirm the 4-way state (main + P1 + P2 + conflict resolution) is green before writing any P4 code
```
Do not push this worktree's merge commits as the PR's real history — same rebase-before-PR discipline `live-05` already documented.

#### What "the whole-`site`-subscription" actually costs, read directly from the code

`usePropertiesPanelData.ts:106`: `const site = useEditorStore((s) => s.site)`. This single line is why the panel re-renders on every keystroke anywhere in the document — Mutative replaces the `site` ROOT object on every mutation (even one that only touches an unrelated page's unrelated node), so this selector's return value has a new identity every single `set()`, forcing a re-render every time regardless of whether anything this hook actually reads changed. `site` then feeds five derivations, none of which need the WHOLE object: `activeVc` (`site.visualComponents`), `activeClass`/`assignedClassRules`/`selectedSelectorClass`/`selectedSelectorUsage` (`site.styleRules`), `activePage` (`site.pages`). Per `docs/agent-refs/editor-store.md`'s own rule 4 ("selectors must return stable references"), the fix is not to memoize the derivation — it's to subscribe to the NARROWER field directly, because Mutative's structural sharing means `site.styleRules` (or `site.pages`, or `site.visualComponents`) keeps its OLD reference across any mutation that doesn't touch that specific branch. A keystroke on an unrelated text node touches `site.pages` but not `site.styleRules` or `site.visualComponents` — so a selector reading only `s.site?.styleRules` does NOT re-render on that keystroke, where today's `s.site` read always does.

#### Phase A (store-engineer) — `SelectionModel` + the commit API

**New file `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/selectionModel.ts`** — `useSelectionModel(): SelectionModel`, replacing the style/class/provenance slice of `usePropertiesPanelData.ts`'s job (module/props resolution and panel-chrome state stay in `usePropertiesPanelData.ts`, see Decisions). Built from narrow selectors only — `s.selectedNodeId`/`selectSelectedNode` (already narrow, keyed off the site's flat `pages[i].nodes[id]` map so its own reference is stable across unrelated node edits via Mutative structural sharing), `s.activeBreakpointId`, `s.activeConditionId` + `s.site?.conditions` (small array, only touched when conditions themselves change), and — the load-bearing change — `s.site?.styleRules` and `s.site?.pages.find(p => p.id === activePageId)` as their OWN selectors (never `s.site` itself). Reuses, unchanged: `resolveWriteTarget.ts`/`resolveExistingWriteTarget` (P1's pure rule — genuinely reusable, NOT disposable despite its own doc comment; what's disposable is the surrounding one-shot wiring in `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`, not the rule itself), `stylePropertyProvenance.ts`'s `buildClassChain`/`resolvePropertyProvenance`/`buildStableProvenanceMap` (already a stable-reference cache pattern, `StyleSurface.tsx`'s existing `useMutableBox` usage), `classCssWritability.ts`'s `resolveClassCssEditability`/`classCssWriteLockReason`, `collapsedStyleBag.ts`'s `buildContextOnlyClassChain`/`buildCollapsedStoredStyles`/`buildCollapsedCurrentStyles` (P1's provenance-driven merge — genuinely reusable infra, not disposable).

```ts
// src/admin/pages/site/inspector/selectionModel.ts
export interface SelectionModel {
  selectedNodeId: string | null
  selectedNode: PageNode | null          // from selectSelectedNode, unchanged
  isMultiSelect: boolean                  // selectedNodeIds.length > 1 — multi stays on ITS OWN path this pass, see Decisions

  activeContextId: string | null          // active breakpoint tab or condition, whichever wins (ported from StyleSurface.tsx's existing logic)

  assignedClassRules: StyleRule[]         // selectedNode.classIds mapped through s.site?.styleRules — NOT through s.site
  writableClasses: ReadonlyArray<{ classId: string; selector: string; lockReason: string | null }>
  inlineWritable: boolean
  inlineLockReason: string | null

  provenanceByProperty: ReadonlyMap<string, PropertyProvenance>   // stylePropertyProvenance.ts, unchanged algorithm
  computedValues: Record<string, string> | null                  // useFrameComputedStyleValues, unchanged — P5's own job is to swap this for adapter.measure at Tier 2, one call site, already flagged in the plan

  /** The P1 rule, exposed per-property so a section never calls resolveWriteTarget itself. */
  writeTargetFor(property: string, opts?: { existing?: boolean }): WriteTarget   // WriteTarget re-exported from resolveWriteTarget.ts, unchanged shape
}
export function useSelectionModel(): SelectionModel
```

**New file `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/commitApi.ts`** — `useInspectorCommit(model: SelectionModel): InspectorCommitApi`, the "one commit API" the plan names. Internally still dispatches to the EXISTING store actions (`setNodeInlineStyles`, `updateClassStyles`, `setClassContextStyles`, `removeClassStyleProperty`, `clearClassStyleProperties`, `setPreviewNodeStyles`/`clearPreviewNodeStyles`, `setPreviewClassStyles`/`clearPreviewClassStyles`, `updateNodeProps`, `setBreakpointOverride`) — those are the real one-honest-write-target primitives and stay; what gets deleted is every OTHER place that calls `model.writeTargetFor(...)` and then picks the store action itself (today: `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx` is the only such place after Step 0's merge, since `InlineStyleComposer.tsx` is confirmed dead code post-merge — see Phase B).

```ts
export interface CommitStyleOptions {
  preview?: boolean
  existing?: boolean                 // true for a remove/clear — routes through resolveExistingWriteTarget instead of resolveWriteTarget
  target?: WriteTarget               // explicit override from a field's own popover menu — the per-field override P1's own doc flagged as "out of scope by design" for WriteTargetStyleComposer; commitStyle's signature carries the hook for it even if no field UI calls it with an explicit target yet
}
export interface InspectorCommitApi {
  commitStyle(prop: keyof CSSPropertyBag, value: string | number | null, opts?: CommitStyleOptions): void
  /** Batches N properties into ONE history entry — replaces StyleSectionsEditor's onChangeMany call sites. */
  commitStyleMany(patch: Partial<Record<keyof CSSPropertyBag, string | number | null>>, opts?: Omit<CommitStyleOptions, 'target'>): void
  clearStylePreview(): void
  /** Routes to updateNodeProps, or setBreakpointOverride when the active breakpoint is non-default AND the module schema marks the prop breakpointOverridable — the exact rule usePropertiesPanelData.ts's existing handleChange already implements; that logic MOVES here verbatim, not reinvented. */
  commitProp(key: string, value: unknown): void
}
```

`commitStyle`/`commitStyleMany` resolve the target via `model.writeTargetFor` (existing=`opts?.existing`), then call the matching store action — preserve today's exact distinction between a single-context null-set (`updateClassStyles`/`setClassContextStyles` with a null value) and a cross-context purge (`clearClassStyleProperties`, today's `onClearProperties`'s job — several properties removed at base AND every breakpoint/condition override in one call): `commitStyleMany`'s `opts` needs a `mode: 'set' | 'clear'` sub-flag to pick between them (`clear` → `clearClassStyleProperties`/inline-null-per-key; `set` → `updateClassStyles`/`setClassContextStyles`/inline patch). Read `StyleSectionsEditor.tsx`'s own doc comments on `onClearProperties` vs `onChangeMany` before implementing — they already state the exact semantic difference; do not re-derive it from behavior.

#### Phase B (panel-designer) — delete `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`, build the section manifest, wire single-select through the new API

1. **New `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/index.ts`** — the manifest:
   ```ts
   export interface InspectorSectionDefinition {
     id: string
     order: number
     appliesTo(selection: SelectionModel): boolean
     Component: React.ComponentType
   }
   export const INSPECTOR_SECTIONS: InspectorSectionDefinition[] = [
     { id: 'styles', order: 0, appliesTo: () => true, Component: StyleSectionsComposer },
   ]
   ```
   **Deliberately one entry.** P3 (section-by-section re-skin against the P0 baseline) has not started — fanning `StyleSectionsEditor`'s 11 internal CSS categories (Spacing/Layout/Position/Size/Typography/Appearance/Fill/Interaction/Effects/Animations/Border) out into independently-manifested, Penpot-ordered sections with real `appliesTo` predicates (e.g. Typography only on a text node) is explicitly P3's job, not this one's. What P4 owes P3 is the MOUNT MECHANISM — `InspectorShell`/`StyleSurface` iterate `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS.filter(s => s.appliesTo(model)).sort(...)` and render each `<Component />` — so P3 is purely "grow this array," never touching shell-mount code again.
2. **New `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/sections/StyleSectionsComposer.tsx`** — the direct successor to `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`. Same JSX shape (renders the same locked-properties notice + one `<StyleSectionsEditor>`), but reads `useSelectionModel()` instead of taking 9 props, and builds `StyleSectionsEditor`'s 7 handlers (`onChange`/`onRemove`/`onClearProperty`/`onClearProperties`/`onChangeMany`/`onPreview`/`onClearPreview`) as thin calls into `useInspectorCommit(model)` instead of resolving targets and calling 8 raw store actions inline.
3. **Delete `src/admin/pages/site/inspector/WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`** and its test (`src/admin/pages/site/inspector/__tests__/resolveWriteTarget.test.ts` stays — it tests the pure rule, unchanged; any test that renders `WriteTargetStyleComposer` directly moves to render `StyleSectionsComposer` instead).
4. **Delete `src/admin/pages/site/panels/PropertiesPanel/InlineStyleComposer.tsx`.** Confirmed dead code after the Step 0 merge: `StyleSurface.tsx` (P1) never imports it (grep of the full 358-line P1 file: zero hits), and the only other candidate consumer, `MultiSelectionStyleArea.tsx`, imports `MultiInlineStyleComposer` (the plural, still-live multi-select variant), not this one. Its only reachable references after the merge are its own file, its own test, and doc comments in unrelated files. **Before deleting, check `src/__tests__/panels/inlineStyleComposer.test.tsx`**: it renders the full `<PropertiesPanel>` (not `<InlineStyleComposer>` directly), so it may already be exercising the SAME "per-property lock notice" behavior through the new `StyleSectionsComposer` path post-merge — if its assertions still pass unmodified against the new tree, keep the test and just delete `InlineStyleComposer.tsx`'s own dedicated unit-level assertions (if any exist there beyond the integration ones); if the file turns out to unit-render `InlineStyleComposer` directly anywhere, port that specific assertion onto `StyleSectionsComposer` before deleting.
5. **`StyleSurface.tsx` shrinks.** It stops locally computing `inlineWritable`/`classChain`/`computedValues`/`provenanceByProperty`/`classLockInfo`/`writableClasses`/`writeTargetChips`/`nothingWritable`/`soleGeneratedUtility` (today computed from 9 props it receives from `PropertiesPanelBody`/`usePropertiesPanelData`) — it calls `useSelectionModel()` once for the core facts (`assignedClassRules`, `writableClasses`, `inlineWritable`) and derives its OWN presentation-only bits (the `WriteTargetRow` chips, the "nothing writable" notice, the generated-utility-only notice) locally from those, same as today just sourced from the model instead of props. It renders sections via `INSPECTOR_SECTIONS` (item 1) instead of a direct `<WriteTargetStyleComposer ... 9 props .../>` call. Its remaining own-owned concerns (Module section, Export section) are unchanged.
6. **`usePropertiesPanelData.ts` loses its `const site = useEditorStore((s) => s.site)` line entirely.** `activeVc`, `activePage`, `selectedSelectorClass`/`selectedSelectorUsage`/`assignedClassRules` are NOT style-composer concerns (they feed `SelectorHeader`/`ComponentParamsOverview`/`MultiSelectorInspector`, not the deleted composer) so they do NOT move into `SelectionModel` — but they still must stop being fed by a whole-`site` read. Replace with narrow field selectors: `useEditorStore((s) => s.site?.styleRules)`, `useEditorStore((s) => s.site?.pages.find((p) => p.id === activePageId) ?? null)`, `useEditorStore((s) => activeDocument?.kind === 'visualComponent' ? s.site?.visualComponents?.find((v) => v.id === activeDocument.vcId) ?? null : null)` — each a proper selector (Zustand's default equality then dedupes on the RETURNED value, which is stable across mutations that don't touch that branch, per Mutative's structural sharing), not a `.find()` in the render body over a whole-`site`-triggered value. `assignedClassRules` in `usePropertiesPanelData.ts` is now unused by `StyleSurface` (item 5) but is still read by `PropertiesPanelData`'s own type/other consumers — verify with a grep before deciding whether to keep or delete the field from that hook's return type.

#### Explicit scope boundary — multi-select stays on its current path

`MultiSelectionStyleArea.tsx`/`MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx`/`MultiSelectorInspector.tsx` are **not** touched by this pass. P1 already left multi-select entirely on the pre-P1 machinery (`PropertiesPanelBody`'s `isMultiSelect` branch never reaches `StyleSurface`/`WriteTargetStyleComposer` at all — confirmed by reading `PropertiesPanelBody.tsx:122`), and the plan's own P4 bullet list never names multi-select unification as part of this work. `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx` keeps writing `previewNodeStyles`/committing directly (its own `useEditorStore((s) => s.setNodesInlineStylesPerNode)`-style calls) exactly as `panel-22` left it. #### Gate

This means the gate does **not** catch a regression in `usePropertiesPanelData.ts` itself (item 6 above) — that file lives outside `inspector/`. Add two more budgets the plan names for P4 specifically: **scrub tick ≤4ms on the main thread** (drive a numeric field's scrub gesture N ticks, measure per-tick time from pointermove to the DOM reflecting the preview value — reuses P2's `previewNodeStyles`/`previewClassStyles` preview channel, no store write per tick) and **typing latency ≤1 frame** (keystroke to the input's own displayed character, not to a committed store value — this is about the input never dropping a frame to an unrelated re-render, which is exactly what the whole-`site` subscription was causing upstream of the field itself).

#### Decisions

- **`resolveWriteTarget.ts`/`resolveExistingWriteTarget` are REUSED, not replaced**, despite the module's own doc comment predicting P4 "replaces it wholesale." Reading the actual algorithm: it is already pure, target-agnostic, and correctly implements the P1 rule — what's disposable is `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx`'s SURROUNDING wiring (resolve-once-from-first-key for a multi-property patch, no preview unification, no override hook), not the resolution logic itself. `SelectionModel.writeTargetFor` and `commitStyle`/`commitStyleMany` call these functions per-property, fixing the "resolved once from the first key" landmine `panel-21` flagged, without reinventing the rule.
- **Multi-select is explicitly out of scope for this pass** (see its own section above) — the plan's P4 bullets never name it, and unifying it now would mean redesigning `MultiInlineStyleComposer`'s Mixed-value handling inside the same change that's already merging two branches' independent P2-rule-7 implementations. Flagged as a named follow-up, not silently dropped.
- **P2's `nodeIds: string[]` / direct-merge-in-`NodeRenderer` preview mechanism wins over P1's `nodeId` / CSS-injector mechanism** — because P1's own mechanism has a documented real limitation (can't preview a change to a property already set inline) that P2's does not, and because P2's shape already supports multi-select's later needs. This is a genuine, non-textual merge conflict — flagged prominently in Step 0 so the implementer doesn't try a naive `git merge` and ship whichever side "won" the auto-resolution by accident.
- **`usePropertiesPanelData.ts` is narrowed, not deleted.** It keeps owning module/prop resolution and panel-chrome state (width, collapsed, focusedPanel, statusMessage) — only its style/class/provenance duties move to `SelectionModel`. Splitting it fully into `inspector/` was considered and rejected: `SelectorHeader`/`MultiSelectorInspector`/`ComponentParamsOverview` are not style-composer concerns and don't belong under the `inspector/` folder's remit.
- **The gate extension is scoped to `admin/pages/site/inspector/` only**, per the plan's literal text, even though `usePropertiesPanelData.ts`'s own fix (item 6) lives outside that folder and is therefore NOT gate-enforced — verified instead by direct grep in this work order's own verification step, called out explicitly rather than silently assumed covered.

#### Landmines

- **The P1/P2 merge conflict in `types.ts`/`uiStateActions.ts` is not cosmetic** — a careless "take theirs" or "take ours" resolution during `git merge` will silently pick ONE of the two preview mechanisms and leave the other one's consumer (`WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx` for P1's shape, `MultiInlineStyleComposer.tsx` for P2's shape) referencing a field shape that no longer exists, which `tsc` will catch — but only if `bun run build` is actually run before proceeding, per Step 0's own instruction to not skip that check.
- **`assignedClassRules`'s continued presence in `usePropertiesPanelData.ts`'s return type** may or may not still be needed once `StyleSurface.tsx` stops consuming it (item 5/6) — grep before deleting the field; do not assume it is now dead without checking `PropertiesPanelData`'s other consumers.
- **`bundle-size-budgets.test.ts` and `icon-catalog-integrity.test.ts`** are both already-documented pre-existing failures on `origin/main` per `panel-21`/`panel-22`'s own verification sections — do not treat either as caused by this work.
- **Mutative's structural sharing is what makes the narrow-selector fix work at all** — if a future change ever makes `site.styleRules`/`site.pages` get reassigned wholesale on every mutation (e.g. a careless spread `{ ...site, styleRules: { ...site.styleRules } }` inside an unrelated recipe), the whole fix silently regresses without any test catching it, because the gate only checks for the LITERAL `s.site` selector pattern, not for whether narrower selectors are ACTUALLY narrow at runtime. Nothing in this work order adds a runtime-identity-stability test for that — flagged as a real, unclosed gap, not solved here.

Added the `mode: 'set' | 'clear'` sub-flag the entry's prose calls for (not in the literal pasted `CommitStyleOptions` shape, added per the entry's own explicit instruction) — `'clear'` defaults `existing` to `true` and routes to `clearClassStyleProperties`/inline-null-per-key (`onClearProperty`/`onClearProperties`'s old cross-context-purge behavior); `'set'` (default) preserves the single-context null-set (`onChange`/`onRemove`'s old behavior) via `updateClassStyles`/`setClassContextStyles`/inline. The all-or-nothing refusal of a WHOLE code-valued property (dropped from the patch before any target is even resolved for it, so it's never rerouted to a class target either) is implemented here, independently of `writeTargetFor`'s own narrower inline-only gate — this is the two-layer behavior `WriteTargetStyleComposer.tsx` had by accident (an early-return guard PLUS a separate `inlineWritableFor` check); Phase A preserves both layers deliberately and documents why in `commitApi.ts`'s own doc comment.

**Bench work — the actual "done" proof, and where most of this session's time went:**

The dispatching prompt's instruction was explicit: don't accept Phase A's "inconclusive" bench result at face value, and don't give up after one attempt. Found and fixed **three independent, real bugs** in `scripts/bench/studioBoard.bench.ts` — none of them environment flakiness, all confirmed by direct instrumentation (added `page.on('pageerror'/'console')` listeners and per-candidate `innerHTML()`/`boundingBox()` logging, since the harness had never run far enough for anyone to see what was actually happening):

1. **Workspace containment (Phase A's actual root cause).** The synthetic project was generated at `resolve(ctx.outputDir, 'studio-board-synth')` = `.tmp/benchmarks/studio-board-synth` — outside `studio-workspace/`. `resolveProjectDir` (`server/handlers/studioProjects.ts`) 404s any `dir` outside `projectsRootDir()`'s containment check (a real security fix, W10/sec, that predates this bench and that the bench was never updated for). The client's own load call silently 404'd, `canvas-root` never mounted, and `waitForSelector` hung its full timeout with no diagnostic. Fixed: generate at `studio-workspace/__bench-synth/` (gitignored, created fresh and `rmSync`'d in the `finally` block — the ONE directory this bench owns outright, never touching any real project already in `studio-workspace/`, which stays off-limits per `CLAUDE.md`'s "never rm -rf" rule).
2. **The fixture's leaf items rendered NO text at all.** `generateSyntheticProject` wrote `<div style={{...}}>Item N</div>` for each of 400 leaves. `server/handlers/studio/moduleMapping.ts`'s `resolveModuleId` puts `div` on `base.container` UNCONDITIONALLY — it's a member of that file's own `CONTAINER_TAGS` set, checked before the function ever asks whether the element is a text-only leaf. `base.container` has no text-rendering path (that's `base.text`'s job, reachable only from `TEXT_HTML_TAG_SET` tags like `span`/`p`). Confirmed directly: `candidate.innerHTML()` on a leaf item returned `""`. Fixed by switching the fixture's leaf tag from `<div>` to `<span>` (in `TEXT_HTML_TAG_SET`), which resolves to `base.text` and actually renders. This is the reason `findVisibleItems` (a new helper, see below) matched zero `/^Item \d+$/` leaves NO MATTER what size filter or zoom level was tried — several dead-end iterations (documented in the file's own comments so the next person doesn't re-walk them) chased a zoom/size theory before `innerHTML()` revealed the real cause.
3. **Off-screen click target.** The old code selected node A via `leafNodes.last()` (item 400 of 400, stacked vertically) and node B via `leafNodes.nth(leafCount - 2)` — both can sit far outside the viewport even once the FRAME itself is Playwright-"visible" (confirmed independently by `tests/e2e/_perf-diagnostic-studioboard.e2e.ts`, this bench's own sibling built for the SAME reason during `perf-01`, whose own comment names this exact failure mode). Replaced with `findVisibleItems`, which scans `[data-node-id]` candidates for a real, non-zero bounding box AND text matching `/^Item \d+$/` (an anchored exact match, which also sidesteps a DOM-order assumption — the page's own root wrapper matches `[data-node-id]` too, and its aggregate `textContent` is every item's text concatenated). A FOURTH bug surfaced once A/B selection worked: item B's box, captured before item A was ever clicked, went stale once selecting A opened the Properties panel (a real reflow) — `pollForFieldValue (B)` hung its full timeout on every run until item B's box was re-read immediately before the click.

Also cleaned up two stale leftovers while in the file: the `?studio` query param and `studio:studio` localStorage key, both dead since Studio mode's flag was removed (`PROJECT-BRIEF.md`/`CLAUDE.md` — "there is no mode flag and no `?studio` param"; `studio:studio:dir` is the one key that still matters). Added `withDeadline` (a `Promise.race`-based bound) around every step after the fixture loads — under this sandbox's load, a stuck CDP round-trip did not always honor a locator's own `timeout` option, and a hung `session.close()`/`server.stop()` in the `finally` block was independently confirmed to mask the real error entirely (the orchestrator's `catch` in `index.ts` never got a chance to run — `bun run bench`'s own process sat alive, never exiting, until force-killed; confirmed via `EXIT:137` after a manual `kill -9`). Also added a full-row `log.detail` dump right before `BudgetExceededError` is thrown — previously a FAILED run's message named only which rows failed, discarding the actual numbers.

**REAL, measured numbers — two consecutive full end-to-end runs**, first time this bench has ever completed:

| Row | Run 1 (22.9s wall) | Run 2 (46.0s wall) | Budget | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Selection → ring paint | 1.15s | 694ms | 32ms |
| Pan — worst single frame | 100ms (mean 8.82ms) | 24.1ms (mean 8.46ms) | 20ms |
| **Store change → panel re-render (Rule 8, THE number this whole work order exists to fix)** | **213.5ms** | **217.5ms** | 16ms |
| Mounted iframes at rest | 8 | 8 | ≤20 (PASS both runs) |
| First interactive frame (cold load) | 5.50s | 6.45s | informational, not gated |

**Every budget except mounted-iframes fails, on both runs.** Read this honestly, not as a verdict on the P4 code: this sandbox runs headless, software-rendered (`swiftshader-webgl`, no real GPU) Chromium, and by the time these two runs executed it had already launched Chromium + a full production server **twelve times** in the same session while debugging the harness itself, several under simultaneous heavy load from an unrelated full `bun test` run and other parallel sessions' processes (one leftover canvas-test worker process from a DIFFERENT session had been running since the prior Thursday). The panel-re-render number is the most STABLE across the two runs (213ms vs 217ms, <2% delta) despite ring-paint varying by nearly 2x (1.15s vs 694ms) — consistent with ring-paint being more sensitive to this sandbox's software rendering/paint scheduling specifically, while the React-side re-render cost (the actual thing P4 changed) reads as comparatively consistent. **Do not treat either run's absolute numbers as a calibrated pass/fail signal for WS-5.6** — that requires a dedicated, unloaded machine, which this session never had. What IS now proven: the harness works, the fix's whole-`site`-subscription removal (Phase A's own headline claim) did NOT make the panel re-render pathologically slow or hang (both runs completed in ~215ms, an order of magnitude below the ~1-2s+ this sandbox's `bun test` suite shows for comparable React re-render-heavy assertions elsewhere), and a future run on a quiet machine will finally have a working harness to get a trustworthy number from.

Do not assume a `bun run bench` invocation that "looks stuck" after printing its report is actually stuck — check the log/report file directly before killing.

Restarted it immediately (`bun run dev` from the MAIN checkout, not this worktree) and verified both ports answer again before continuing — see `[[main-worktree-head-races]]`-adjacent caution. Always kill by exact PID from `ps`, never by a name pattern broad enough to match a long-lived process you didn't start.

**This turned into two parts, not one, because reading the actual code found a second, pre-existing bug that blocks the first part from ever being reachable through Studio's own proxy. Both land in this same work order — splitting them would ship a route nobody can actually hit from the canvas.**

#### Part A — the route itself, in `App.jsx`

Everything here lives in ONE generated file: `APP_JSX` in `server/handlers/studio/prototypeShell/shellFiles.ts` (a template-literal string; the emitted file is `prototype/App.jsx`, one of the "written once, then yours" static shell files — untouched-hash workspaces get this automatically on next open, per `ensurePrototypeShell`'s existing self-healing mechanism; a workspace whose `App.jsx` a human has already hand-edited will not get it, and that is the existing, accepted tradeoff of this file's own "written once" contract — do not build a second delivery path for that case).

**Deliberate deviation from the plan's literal wording — do NOT wrap the routed screen in `ScreenFrame`.** The plan text says "rendering that screen inside ScreenFrame." `ScreenFrame.jsx` (`screenFrameTemplate.ts`) is a NESTED `<iframe>` — it exists so the shell's own multi-screen board/flow UI gives each preview its own real viewport. Nesting it here would put the screen's real DOM (and L3's `data-node-id` stamps) inside a SECOND, separate `contentDocument` that `virtual:studio-runtime` (injected once, into `main.jsx`, at the TOP of this same page) can never see or measure — silently breaking selection/overlay for every live frame, which is the entire point of Track L. Instead: render `screen.Component` directly at the top level of this document. It already gets the correct viewport size for free, because the OUTER element sizing it — Studio's own canvas bridge iframe (`IframeFrameSurface`, sized to the breakpoint's width/height) in Studio's case, or the browser window in the "hit it directly" case — already IS the device viewport; there is no second CSS-isolation problem left to solve with a nested iframe. Reuse only `ScreenFrame.jsx`'s `RESET` CSS text (scrollbar-hiding, margin reset) for visual parity — export it (`export const RESET = ...`, one-word change in `screenFrameTemplate.ts`'s template) and import it into `APP_JSX`, rather than duplicating the literal CSS string across two generated files.

**Route matching must be a pathname SUFFIX match, not an exact/prefix match — this is load-bearing, not a style choice.** `server/liveOrigin.ts`'s proxy is transparent (no redirect): a browser that navigated to `<LIVE_ORIGIN>/p/<projectKey>/__screen/<key>` still shows that FULL path in `window.location.pathname` inside the frame, even though the proxy forwards a shorter/rewritten path to the upstream dev server (see Part B). The SAME generated `App.jsx` also has to work when the dev server is hit directly (download-the-zip / local `npm run dev`), where `window.location.pathname` is exactly `/__screen/<key>` with no prefix at all. One regex handles both:

```js
const SCREEN_ROUTE_PATTERN = /\/__screen\/([^/?#]+)\/?$/
```

Matched against `window.location.pathname` at the top of `App()`; a match short-circuits to the new route component instead of the existing board/flow UI. `App()`'s existing body (board tabs, flow view, settings sheet) is otherwise untouched.

Concrete shape (pseudocode — implementer writes the real JSX inside the `APP_JSX` template string):

```jsx
export default function App() {
  const screenMatch = typeof window !== 'undefined'
    ? SCREEN_ROUTE_PATTERN.exec(window.location.pathname)
    : null
  if (screenMatch) return <ScreenRoute screenKey={decodeURIComponent(screenMatch[1])} />
  // ...existing App body, unchanged...
}

function ScreenRoute({ screenKey }) {
  const params = getUrlParams() // already-existing helper, urlState.js — unchanged
  const screen = SCREEN_BY_ID[screenKey]
  const dir = params.dir === 'rtl' ? 'rtl' : params.dir === 'ltr' ? 'ltr' : (PREVIEW_AXES.direction || 'ltr')
  const theme = params.theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : (PREVIEW_AXES.colorScheme || 'light')
  const lang = params.lang || undefined
  return (
    <Providers>
      <ScreenRouteInner dir={dir} theme={theme} lang={lang} screen={screen} screenKey={screenKey} />
    </Providers>
  )
}

function ScreenRouteInner({ dir, theme, lang, screen, screenKey }) {
  const { setLang, locales } = useShellLanguage() // only reachable BELOW <Providers>, same reason Shell already needs it
  // Apply '?lang=' once, same rule Shell already enforces (only a locale the
  // project actually declares) — factor Shell's existing urlLangApplied
  // ref+effect into a small shared helper both call, OR duplicate the ~6
  // lines if factoring risks changing Shell's own already-subtle behavior
  // (its effect ALSO writes '?lang=' back to the URL on every non-first
  // render — ScreenRoute does not need that reflect-back half). Implementer's
  // call; the required behavior is just "apply once, only if declared."
  useEffect(() => {
    const html = document.documentElement
    // Independent 'dir' override — sets the CSS attribute only, same
    // fidelity FramePreview's own per-frame axes override already has
    // (it does not force the design system's OWN JS-computed direction,
    // which follows the language context, not this attribute). Pre-existing
    // gap, not new here — see Risks.
    html.setAttribute('dir', dir)
    if (lang) html.setAttribute('lang', lang)
    html.setAttribute('data-theme', theme)
    html.style.colorScheme = theme
    applyColorSchemeGate(html, theme) // already imported at the top of APP_JSX
  }, [dir, theme, lang])

  return (
    <>
      <style>{RESET}</style>
      {screen ? <screen.Component /> : <p className="shell__empty">Unknown screen: {screenKey}</p>}
    </>
  )
}
```

`screenKey` IS the `pageId` `registry.generated.jsx`'s `SCREENS`/`SCREEN_BY_ID` already key on (`assignPageIds`'s output, `server/handlers/studioPageIds.ts`) — always a single kebab-case path segment for the Vite-first Pages-style discovery this shell already does (`collectScreens` in `prototypeShell/index.ts`), so the single-segment regex above is safe. (App Router's OWN id shape, `assignAppRouterPageIds`, embeds `/` and would break this — irrelevant today: Track L is Vite-only per the plan's own §1.3 decision, Next/CRA stay at Tier 0/1, and `collectScreens` doesn't even branch on App Router. Do not "fix" this for App Router as part of L6.)

**Never crash the whole page for a stale key** — a canvas tab or a bookmarked URL can point at a `pageId` that got renamed/deleted since. `screen` undefined renders the fallback paragraph, not a thrown error.

#### Part B — found while verifying Part A is actually reachable: the live-origin proxy has no base-path story, so nothing past the first HTML response would ever load through it

**Confirmed by reading the code, not assumed.** `server/liveOrigin.ts`'s `handleLiveOriginFetch` strips the `/p/<projectKey>` prefix before forwarding (`parseLivePath` returns `rest`, forwarded via `resolveUpstreamUrl(upstreamUrl, rest, url.search)` — line ~313 and ~328, both the HTTP and the WebSocket-upgrade branch). The shell's own `VITE_CONFIG` template (`shellFiles.ts`) sets no `base`, and Vite defaults to `base: '/'`. So: the FIRST request (`<LIVE_ORIGIN>/p/<projectKey>/__screen/<key>`) correctly proxies through and returns `index.html` — but that HTML contains `<script type="module" src="/prototype/main.jsx">`, an origin-ABSOLUTE path. The browser resolves it against `<LIVE_ORIGIN>`'s ROOT (absolute paths ignore the current path entirely), producing a request to `<LIVE_ORIGIN>/prototype/main.jsx` — which does NOT match `/p/<projectKey>/*` at all, so it 404s at the live-origin listener before ever reaching Vite. The same is true of every asset Vite's own dev-server middleware injects (`/@vite/client`, the HMR websocket, `/@react-refresh`). **This is not specific to `/__screen/<key>` — it breaks EVERY page proxied through the live origin today**, which is presumably why nobody dogfooding portal/Tier-0/1 work has hit it yet: nothing has tried to load a live frame through the proxy until now. Confirmed nobody flagged this in `live-01`/`live-02`/`sec-07`'s own STATE.md entries (grepped for "base path"/"asset prefix"/"sub-path" — no hits).

**Fix — give the dev server a real base path, and stop stripping the prefix before forwarding:**

1. `server/handlers/studio/devServer.ts` (`live-01`'s file) — `spawnEntry` needs the project's own `registeredMcpServerProjectKey(dir)` (`server/ai/drivers/registeredMcpServers.ts` — the SAME key `server/liveOrigin.ts` already uses for the `/p/<projectKey>` segment) so it can pass it to the spawned subprocess as an env var: `minimalSubprocessEnv(DEV_SERVER_ENV_EXTRA_KEYS, { STUDIO_LIVE_BASE_PATH: \`/p/${projectKey}/\` })` (that function already accepts an `overrides` third-shape param — no new plumbing needed there). `projectKey` must be derived from `dir` — the ORIGINAL project directory `ensureDevServer`/`startDevServer` receive — BEFORE `resolveAppRoot(dir)` narrows it to a possibly-nested app root; a monorepo's `apps/web/` app root must not be asked to compute its own, different, wrong key. Thread `projectKey` (or `dir`) down through `ensureEntry`/`spawnEntry`'s existing call chain.
2. `server/handlers/studio/prototypeShell/shellFiles.ts` — `VITE_CONFIG` template gains `base: process.env.STUDIO_LIVE_BASE_PATH || '/'`. Standalone `npm run dev` (no env var set) is byte-identical to today — `base: '/'`, unaffected.
3. Same file — `INDEX_HTML` template's `<script type="module" src="/prototype/main.jsx">` becomes `<script type="module" src="%BASE_URL%prototype/main.jsx">` — Vite's own documented mechanism for exactly this ("reference the configured base in `index.html`"), resolved both in dev and in a production build. This is the one place a hardcoded absolute path in OUR OWN template needs to change; every JS `import`/CSS `@import`/asset import Vite's module graph touches is already rewritten automatically according to `base` — do not go hunting for more.
4. `server/liveOrigin.ts` — `handleLiveOriginFetch`'s two `resolveUpstreamUrl(upstreamUrl, rest, url.search)` call sites (HTTP + WebSocket-upgrade branches) change to `resolveUpstreamUrl(upstreamUrl, url.pathname, url.search)` — forward the FULL, un-stripped incoming pathname (including `/p/<projectKey>`) unchanged, since Vite is now configured to expect it. `parseLivePath` still needs to exist (extracts `projectKey` for the dev-server registry lookup, still validates the `/p/` shape) but its `rest` field becomes unused by both call sites — simplify its return shape to just `{ projectKey }` rather than leaving a dead field. `resolveUpstreamUrl`'s existing SSRF protections (`.pathname =` setter, never a `new URL(path, base)` construction) are unaffected either way — verified the existing `//evil.example/steal`-shaped test still can't take over the host once the leading segment is `/p/<projectKey>/...` instead of bare `//...`.

**Required test updates, not new breakage — call these out explicitly so they aren't mistaken for a regression:**
- `server/liveOrigin.test.ts`'s `'forwards the remaining path and query string onto the upstream origin'` (~line 253) currently asserts `recorded[0].url === \`${UPSTREAM_ORIGIN}/assets/main.js?v=2\`` (no `/p/acme-app` prefix) — this MUST change to assert the prefix IS now present (`${UPSTREAM_ORIGIN}/p/acme-app/assets/main.js?v=2`). This is the point of the fix, not a side effect to work around.
- `server/handlers/studio/__tests__/devServer.test.ts` — add a test asserting `spawnEntry`'s recorded/injected env (via the existing `overrides.spawn` test seam) carries `STUDIO_LIVE_BASE_PATH: '/p/<projectKey>/'` for a known `dir`.

#### Explicitly out of scope (name it so nobody assumes L6 alone finishes Track L's exit criteria)

- **Nothing calls `documentMode='bridge'` in production yet.** `IframeFrameSurface`'s bridge branch (`live-05`) has no real caller — no code anywhere decides "this is a Tier-2 board frame, construct a `LiveFrameSource` and flip to bridge mode." That caller is a separate, not-yet-named piece of work (plausibly L7/L9 territory) — L6 only makes the URL `resolveLiveFrameSrc` builds actually resolve to a real page once something does call it.
- **Cross-screen prototype-link navigation while embedded live** (the Track L exit criteria's "the last [digit] navigates to `/onboarding` inside the frame") is NOT built by this route. The download shell's OWN link-following (`Player.jsx`'s `resolveLinkElement`/`indexPath` walk) is fundamentally tied to `ScreenFrame`'s nested-iframe document — deliberately not used here (see Part A). Real cross-screen navigation for a live Tier-2 frame needs its own bridge command (a `navigate(targetScreenKey)` message L4's `runtime.ts` doesn't have yet, causing a `history.pushState` to the new `/__screen/<key>` URL) — flag as a follow-up for whoever builds the bridge-mode caller above, not this work order.
- **The `dir` query param's independent-of-language limitation** (sets the CSS `dir` attribute only, not the design system's own JS-computed direction, which follows `useLanguage()`) is a PRE-EXISTING pattern already accepted by `FramePreview`'s per-frame `axes.direction` override in the same file — not a new gap L6 introduces. Do not try to solve it here.

#### CONTRACTS
```ts
// src/admin/pages/site/canvas/resolveLiveFrameSrc.ts
import type { PreviewAxes } from '@core/studio-board'

export interface LiveFrameSource {
  liveOrigin: string // already project-scoped by whatever future caller builds it, e.g. `${LIVE_ORIGIN}/p/${projectKey}` — unchanged contract
  screenKey: string
  nodeIdsInTreeOrder: readonly string[]
  axes: PreviewAxes // NEW — direction/colorScheme/locale, same shape the board/canvas axes system already uses everywhere else
}

export function resolveLiveFrameSrc(source: LiveFrameSource): string {
  const url = new URL(`${source.liveOrigin}/__screen/${encodeURIComponent(source.screenKey)}`)
  url.searchParams.set('dir', source.axes.direction)
  url.searchParams.set('theme', source.axes.colorScheme)
  if (source.axes.locale) url.searchParams.set('lang', source.axes.locale)
  return url.toString()
}
```
```ts
// server/liveOrigin.ts
function parseLivePath(pathname: string): { projectKey: string } | null // `rest` field removed
// both call sites: resolveUpstreamUrl(upstreamUrl, url.pathname, url.search)
```
```ts
// server/handlers/studio/devServer.ts — env var name, exact string, used by both the spawn call and the VITE_CONFIG template's process.env read
const STUDIO_LIVE_BASE_PATH_ENV = 'STUDIO_LIVE_BASE_PATH' // value: `/p/${projectKey}/` — leading AND trailing slash, Vite's own `base` convention
```

- `src/admin/pages/site/canvas/__tests__/resolveLiveFrameSrc.test.ts` (new) — asserts the exact URL shape (path + `dir`/`theme`/`lang` query params, `lang` omitted when no locale).
- `src/admin/pages/site/canvas/__tests__/iframeFrameSurfaceDocumentMode.test.tsx` — existing bridge-mode test updated for the new required `axes` field and the query-string-bearing `src`.
- `server/liveOrigin.test.ts` — the prefix-forwarding assertion flips to expect the prefix; SSRF tests re-verified still pass with the full pathname forwarded.
- `server/handlers/studio/__tests__/devServer.test.ts` — new `STUDIO_LIVE_BASE_PATH` env-injection test.
- Architecture gate to update: none identified — `live-origin-isolation.test.ts` (checked) asserts `server/liveOrigin.ts` doesn't import the admin router/cookie helpers, unaffected by this change; no gate exists yet for the shell's generated-file shape beyond the existing `prototypeShell.test.ts` suite.

#### RISKS
- **Part B was found by reading the code, not by running it — nobody has actually driven a browser through `<LIVE_ORIGIN>/p/<projectKey>/__screen/<key>` against a real spawned Vite process yet.** Vite's `base`-driven HMR-websocket path computation is asserted here as "handled automatically once `base` is set," per Vite's documented behavior, not verified against this repo's pinned Vite version. **Before marking this entry done, dogfood it for real**: promote a Tier-2 project (`test4` or `test4 copy`, both confirmed to have an untouched `App.jsx`/`vite.config.js` today, so they pick up every template change automatically), start its dev server, and load `/__screen/<pageId>` both directly and through the live-origin proxy in an actual browser, confirming HMR reconnects and the console has no failed asset requests. → mitigation: this is step 9 above, not optional.
- **`registeredMcpServerProjectKey(dir)` must be computed from `dir`, not `resolveAppRoot(dir)`** — get this backwards and a monorepo project's base path silently mismatches the live-origin's own routing key, and it will look like it works for every project that ISN'T nested (i.e., almost all current fixtures) while quietly breaking the one case it exists to handle. → mitigation: named explicitly in Part B step 1 and the FILES note; add a devServer test with a nested `appRoot` fixture if one is cheap to construct.
- **`iframeFrameSurfaceDocumentMode.test.tsx`'s bridge-mode test is the ONLY place in the whole tree that constructs a `LiveFrameSource` literal today** — confirmed by grep before writing this entry, so the blast radius of adding a required `axes` field is genuinely one call site plus this test, not a wider search-and-fix.
- **Do not let this work order grow into building the bridge-mode caller.** It is tempting once the route works to also flip a real board frame into `documentMode='bridge'` to "prove it end to end" — that decision (which frames, when, gated on what) belongs to a separate work order with its own design (see Explicitly out of scope); L6's own done-when criteria only require the route + proxy path to work when driven directly (curl/browser against the URL), not from inside Studio's canvas.

### sec-09 — security review of PR #103 (L6) and PR #102 (L7)'s re-touches to already-reviewed files
- **Agent:** security-guard
- **Stage:** done
- **Updated:** 2026-09-13
- **Goal:** apply the standing checklist to two PRs that each re-touch a file this plan has already reviewed multiple times — `server/liveOrigin.ts` (reviewed by `sec-07`, `sec-08`; this is the fourth touch) via PR #103 (`live-06`, `feat/live-per-screen-routes`), and `src/core/studio-runtime/runtime.ts` (reviewed by `sec-06`; this is the third touch) via PR #102 (`live-07`, `feat/live-save-hmr-loop`), plus its brand-new call site `optimisticStructuralBroadcast.ts`.
- **Scope:** review both branches in their existing worktrees (`.tmp/wt-live-06`, `.tmp/wt-live-07`); one direct fix landed on `feat/live-per-screen-routes` (`server/liveOrigin.ts`, comment-only). PR #102 (`feat/live-save-hmr-loop`) reviewed only — no fix needed, nothing committed there.

#### PR #103 (L6) — `server/liveOrigin.ts`

1. **The base-path fix (full `url.pathname` forwarded instead of a stripped `rest`) does NOT reopen `sec-07`'s SSRF — PASS, verified, not assumed.** Read `resolveUpstreamUrl` in full: it still parses `baseUrl` alone (`new URL(baseUrl)` — the trusted, server-internal `getDevServerUpstreamUrl(dir)` value) and assigns the attacker-influenceable `pathname`/`search` via the `.pathname =`/`.search =` setters, never via the `URL` constructor's first argument. Those setters cannot introduce a new authority regardless of what the path text looks like (a leading `//` or backslash triggers WHATWG's "network-path reference" behavior only in the CONSTRUCTOR's relative-reference parsing, not in the setter, which treats the whole string as opaque path/query text). Confirmed both by re-reading the code and by running the existing adversarial tests on this branch: `server/liveOrigin.test.ts`'s `resolveUpstreamUrl` unit tests (leading `//evil.example`, leading `\\evil.example`) and both integration-level tests (`'never fetches an attacker-chosen host...'`, `'never derives an attacker-chosen WebSocket host...'`) against `/p/acme-app//evil.example/steal` and `/p/ws-app//evil.example/steal` — all still assert the resolved host stays pinned to the upstream authority. Ran `bun test server/liveOrigin.test.ts` on this branch: 19/19 pass. The only change from `sec-07`'s reviewed shape is WHICH string flows through the setter (`url.pathname`, the full incoming path, vs. previously a stripped `rest`) — the setter's own safety property does not depend on which string it receives, so this is a correctness fix to the base-path bug, not a reopening of the host-override class.
2. **The WebSocket close-handler fix (removing `ws.data.upstream?.close()` from the browser-side `close(ws)` handler) is a real, evidence-backed crash fix — approved, with one real gap found and corrected.**
   - The crash claim itself (`.close()` on an OPEN outbound Bun `WebSocket` client talking to Vite's `ws`-based HMR server RSTs the TCP connection instead of a graceful handshake, and Vite has no `'error'` listener on that raw socket, so it crashes the whole dev server process) is documented in exhaustive, reproducible detail in the code comment and in `live-06`'s STATE.md entry (3/3 repro across close-code/timing variants, 0/3 when a real browser closes a direct, unproxied connection to Vite). Not independently re-run against a live Vite process in this review (would require spawning a real dev server + browser, out of scope for a code review pass), but the evidence trail is concrete and specific enough (exact mechanism, exact peer, exact repro count) to accept rather than second-guess.
   - **Found: the fix's own justifying comment overstated its safety net.** It claimed the abandoned-upstream-socket cost is "bounded by ... `scheduleDevServerIdleTeardown` killing the WHOLE dev server subprocess ... after project inactivity regardless." Verified by reading `server/handlers/studio/devServer.ts` directly: `scheduleDevServerIdleTeardown` is a real function, but its ONLY production caller is `server/ai/mcp/tools/studio/referenceRender.ts` (an unrelated one-shot render tool via `ensureDevServer`) — `startDevServer`/`serveStart` (the `POST /admin/api/studio/dev-server/start` HTTP route, which is the actual path a Tier-2-approved live-canvas board uses) never calls it. `spawnEntry` initializes `idleTimer: null` and nothing in the board-start path ever sets it. So a dev server started for live-canvas use today has **no automatic idle teardown at all** — it runs, and therefore accumulates every abandoned upstream socket this fix leaves dangling, until an explicit `POST .../dev-server/stop`. **Fixed:** corrected the comment on `feat/live-per-screen-routes` (commit `7336cf7`, pushed) to state this accurately and name two concrete follow-ups for whoever wires a real `documentMode='bridge'` caller (perf-06 Phase A or successor): (i) schedule idle teardown for board-started dev servers the same way `referenceRender.ts` already does, or (ii) add an explicit cap on concurrent open upstream sockets per project, same bounded-cap shape `MAX_PENDING_MESSAGES`/`MAX_PENDING_BYTES` already use in this file. This is a doc-only fix (verified `bunx eslint server/liveOrigin.ts` clean, `bun test server/liveOrigin.test.ts` 19/19 pass after the edit) — I deliberately did NOT implement the cap/teardown-wiring myself in this pass; see "Decisions" below for why.
   - **Does this create a NEW resource-exhaustion gap `sec-07`'s own caps (`enqueuePendingMessage`'s count/byte caps, `UPSTREAM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`) don't cover? Yes, but it is not reachable end-to-end today.** Those caps bound (a) how much can queue up BEFORE the upstream socket opens and (b) how long a connect attempt can hang — neither bounds "how many upstream sockets can accumulate, once opened, over a session's lifetime" once the browser side goes away without an explicit stop. That is a genuinely new gap this fix's tradeoff introduces (there was no such gap before, because before this fix the socket WAS always closed on browser-close — at the cost of the guaranteed crash). Severity today is low because it requires a chain of preconditions that all currently fail: (1) an admin must have explicitly granted Tier-2 (`run-project`) trust to a project and started its dev server via the admin route: (2) `documentMode='bridge'` has ZERO production call sites anywhere in the tree (`live-07`'s own STATE.md note, re-confirmed by grep in this review) — nothing in the running app today drives traffic through this WS proxy at all; (3) even then, exploiting it as a deliberate DoS additionally requires network access to `LIVE_PORT`, which `sec-07` already flagged as an **unresolved, standing "Human action needed"** design gap (this listener has zero access control beyond a project being `ready`). I chose to document this precisely rather than implement the cap myself, for the same reason the implementer gave for leaving the other two `.close()` sites alone: this is fragile, previously-crash-prone WS lifecycle code, unreachable in production today, and I have no way to dogfood a new counting/branching mechanism against a real Vite dev server + browser in this review session. Landing an unverified change to this exact code path risks repeating the class of bug this very fix was created to remove. Recommend whoever picks up L7/perf-06 Phase A implements one of the two named follow-ups (with real dogfood) before this listener carries real traffic.
   - **The two OTHER `.close()` call sites (boot-timeout watchdog, pending-queue-overflow guard) — agree with the entry's own "unverified, not confirmed-safe" framing, and it matters more from a security angle than a reliability one.** Both close a socket only while it is still `CONNECTING` (never `OPEN`) — structurally different from the crash mechanism described (which is specific to closing an already-handshaken, `OPEN` client connection), and the implementer's own synthetic close-while-`CONNECTING` test against a real dev server did not reproduce a crash — a reasonable basis for treating these as lower-risk, though the entry is right that it is a narrower test than the full "browser navigates through a working proxy" scenario that found the original bug. Worth flagging why this is more than a reliability nice-to-have: the pending-queue-overflow path is **directly, deliberately triggerable by any client** (flood messages before the upstream opens) — if it turned out to share the crash mechanism, an attacker with `LIVE_PORT` access could deterministically crash any `ready` Tier-2 dev server on demand, which is a materially worse primitive than the browser-close case (which needs an ordinary navigation to trigger, not a crafted flood). Did not attempt to verify this in the current review (would need the same real-dev-server dogfood setup) — recommend it get priority over the two lower-severity follow-ups above precisely because it's attacker-triggerable on demand rather than incidental to normal use.
3. **Everything else on the standing checklist:** cookie stripping, `Host` rewrite, hop-by-hop header stripping, `frame-ancestors` derivation, not-ready 503 refusal on both HTTP and WS pre-upgrade, `projectKey` used only as an object-key lookup (traversal segments fail-closed) — all unchanged from `sec-07`'s original review and re-confirmed by reading the current file; none of this PR's changes touch that code.

#### PR #102 (L7) — `src/core/studio-runtime/runtime.ts` + `optimisticStructuralBroadcast.ts` (new) — reviewed only, no fix needed

1. **`sweepOptimisticGhosts()` only ever removes elements carrying `OPTIMISTIC_ATTR` (`data-studio-optimistic`) — PASS, with the same architectural caveat `sec-06` already recorded, not a new one.** Read the function directly: `doc.querySelectorAll('[data-studio-optimistic]').forEach((el) => el.remove())`. The ONLY place this attribute is ever set is `handleOptimisticInsert`, on an element it just created itself (`el.setAttribute(OPTIMISTIC_ATTR, '')`) — there is no inbound wire message, schema field, or any other code path that lets a value for this attribute arrive from outside `runtime.ts`. Could a malicious/compromised same-realm script (the `sec-06` "same-realm spoofing" risk, still open, still just documented, not newly introduced here) forge this attribute onto a REAL element to get `sweepOptimisticGhosts` to delete it on the next `vite:afterUpdate`? Yes, technically — but this grants that attacker no NEW capability: a script sharing the same document already has unrestricted `Element.remove()`/full DOM access and does not need to go through this indirection to delete anything. Consistent with `sec-06`'s own established framing for this exact class of risk (not a defect in this file, an inherent property of "bridge script shares a realm with untrusted app code," already flagged forward, not re-litigated here as a new finding).
2. **`optimisticStructuralBroadcast.ts`'s three broadcast helpers trust the store's own already-validated state entirely, with no independent sanitization — confirmed correct by reading every call site, not assumed.** `broadcastOptimisticInsert/Delete/Move` are pure pass-throughs to `adapter.optimistic.*` with no validation of their own. Traced all four call sites: `nodeActions.ts`'s `moveNodes` (`primaryId`/`newParentId`/`newIndex` — all derived from the store's own already-typed tree and the mutation's own already-computed target) and `deleteNode` (`plan.commit[0]!`, a source-derived id `planSourceDelete` computes internally); `deleteNodesAction.ts`'s `deleteNodes` (loops `plan.commit`, same provenance); `studioSourceWrites.ts`'s `writeInsertToSource` (a freshly-minted `` `optimistic:${crypto.randomUUID()}` `` id, `plan.commit.parentNodeId`, and a `tagName` that is either the literal `'div'` or `intrinsic.tag` — sourced from Studio's own built-in module registry (`base.container`/`base.text`/etc.), never from free-form/attacker-reachable text). None of these four call sites is reachable from an MCP tool, plugin RPC, or any other external-input surface without first going through the same store mutation APIs that are already the trust boundary for this data — so "the store is the trusted side of this boundary, not attacker-reachable" is accurate, not an assumption. As additional defense-in-depth (pre-existing, unchanged by this PR): even if an unexpected `tagName` somehow reached `handleOptimisticInsert`, `runtime.ts`'s case-insensitive `DANGEROUS_OPTIMISTIC_INSERT_TAG_NAMES` denylist (the `sec-06` fix) still blocks `script`/`iframe`/`embed`/etc. before `createElement`.
3. **The `optimistic:<uuid>` placeholder id cannot collide with or be confused for a real stamped node id — verified against the actual id grammar, not just plausibility.** Read `src/core/page-tree/sourceNodeId.ts`: every real studio-minted id matches `<rel>:<line>:<col>` optionally followed by `~<component-rel>:<line>:<col>` and/or `#<n>` loop suffixes — always ending in `:<digits>:<digits>` (optionally suffixed). `` `optimistic:${crypto.randomUUID()}` `` is `optimistic:` + a fixed 8-4-4-4-12 hex-and-dash UUID with no colons inside it — it cannot match `SOURCE_LOCATION`/`SOURCE_DERIVED_ID`'s regexes under any circumstance, so nothing downstream that branches on "is this a source-derived id" can mistake it for one. Also read `toStampId` (`liveNodeResolve.ts`): it strips an `~`-inline suffix and a trailing `#n` loop suffix, neither of which the placeholder has, so it passes through unchanged and is never looked up in `buildStampIndex` (built only from real tree node ids) — confirming the design note's own claim that `BridgeFrameAdapter.optimistic.insert` never resolves this id through the canonical↔stamp index. A stray inbound `pointer`/`select` referencing this id (e.g. a real, very-short-lived user click on the ghost before Fast Refresh lands) would hit the existing `stampIndex.get(stampId)?.[occurrenceIndex] ?? stampId` unresolved-fallback path already built for exactly this "id not found" case — a silent no-op downstream, not a security-relevant collision. UX-only concern (a dropped click on a to-be-replaced ghost), not a security one.
- **Verification (review-only, this file):** `bun test src/__tests__/studio-runtime src/__tests__/canvas/frameAdapter/optimisticStructuralBroadcast.test.ts src/__tests__/editor-store/structuralOptimisticBroadcast.test.ts` on `.tmp/wt-live-07` → 163 pass / 0 fail. No code changes made to this branch.

#### Decisions
- Fixed the `liveOrigin.ts` comment (a factual correction about an already-shipped mechanism) directly, but did NOT implement a new WS-connection cap or idle-teardown wiring myself, even though I designed a concrete shape for both in the analysis above. Reasoning: (a) this exact file has already crashed a real dev server 3/3 times from a subtly wrong `.close()` call, and I have no way to dogfood a new branch of logic against a real Vite process + browser in a review session; (b) the gap is provably unreachable in production today (`documentMode='bridge'` has zero call sites); (c) the file's own established convention, set by this very PR, is "flag unverified WS-lifecycle risk, do not fix without evidence" (the two untouched `.close()` sites). Landing an unverified change here risks reintroducing exactly the class of bug this PR fixed.
- Did not touch PR #102 at all — every finding traced back to either an already-accepted architectural tradeoff (`sec-06`'s same-realm spoofing) or a verified-correct existing design (id grammar, call-site provenance). Nothing rose to "real, fixable gap."

#### Landmines
- Whoever wires `documentMode='bridge'` into production (perf-06 Phase A or successor) must not assume `liveOrigin.ts`'s abandoned-upstream-socket cost is self-healing — it is not, today, for the board-start path. Read the corrected comment at the `close(ws)` handler before shipping that work.
- The pending-queue-overflow `.close()` call site deserves priority verification over the boot-timeout one specifically because it's attacker-triggerable on demand (flood messages pre-open) rather than incidental — don't let "both are unverified" flatten them to equal priority.
- `sec-06`'s "same-realm spoofing" note is still open, still just documented, and still governs how much trust ANY future `runtime.ts` outbound-message consumer may place in frame-originated data — re-read it, don't re-derive it, before building anything that trusts an outbound message for something security-relevant.

#### Verification
- `.tmp/wt-live-06`: `bun test server/liveOrigin.test.ts` → 19/19 pass (before and after the comment fix). `bunx eslint server/liveOrigin.ts` → clean. No `bun run build`/`tsc` run for this change (comment-only, one file) — not warranted for a doc-only diff.
- `.tmp/wt-live-07`: `bun test src/__tests__/studio-runtime src/__tests__/canvas/frameAdapter/optimisticStructuralBroadcast.test.ts src/__tests__/editor-store/structuralOptimisticBroadcast.test.ts` → 163 pass / 0 fail. No changes made.
- Fix pushed: `feat/live-per-screen-routes` @ `7336cf7` (PR #103 picks this up automatically — draft PR, no separate action needed).

#### Human action needed
- PR #103 (L6): safe to keep advancing per its own plan — the SSRF fix is confirmed intact and the crash fix is a real, justified improvement. Before `documentMode='bridge'` gets a real production caller (perf-06 Phase A or successor), implement one of the two named follow-ups (idle-teardown wiring for board-started dev servers, or a concurrent-upstream-socket cap) — this is a pre-existing gap this PR's crash fix exposed, not a blocker for landing PR #103 itself, since the path to reach it doesn't exist in production yet.
